They are responsible for complying with the demand, following which their current clearance or departure permission becomes void.
Agent: A written demand for the return of port clearance or departure permission may be legally served by delivering the notice to the agent of the person in charge of the conveyance.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Exemption of certain classes of conveyance from certain provisions of this Chapter
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
59. Exemption of certain classes of conveyance from certain provisions of this Chapter.- (1) The provisions of sections 44, 52 and 54 shall not apply to a conveyance other than a vessel which carries no goods other than the baggage of its occupants.
(2) The 2[Government] may, by notification in the official Gazette, exempt conveyances belonging to Government or any foreign Government from all or any of the provisions of this Chapter.

Conveyance: Certain provisions of this chapter do not apply to conveyances, other than vessels, that are exclusively carrying the baggage of their occupants.

The Government has the authority to issue notifications in the official Gazette to exempt conveyances belonging to the Government or foreign Governments from all or specific provisions of this chapter.
Government: The Government is empowered to grant exemptions to government-owned or foreign government-owned conveyances from the provisions of this chapter through an official Gazette notification.

processed_clauses.metadata_title: CHAPTER VIII - GENERAL PROVISIONS AFFECTING CONVEYANCES AT CUSTOMS-STATIONS
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
CHAPTER VIII
GENERAL PROVISIONS AFFECTING CONVEYANCES
AT CUSTOMS-STATIONS

Conveyance: This chapter establishes general legal provisions and regulatory oversight applicable to all conveyances arriving at or departing from customs-stations.
Customs Station: These provisions define the scope of regulatory authority and operational rules governing the movement and handling of conveyances at designated customs-stations.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to depute officers of customs to board conveyances
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 60. Power to depute officers of customs to board conveyances.- At any time while a conveyance is in a customs-station or is proceeding towards such station, the appropriate officer may depute one or more officers of customs to board the conveyance, and every officer so deputed shall remain on board such conveyance for such time as the appropriate officer may consider necessary.

Conveyance: A customs officer has the authority to board a conveyance at any time while it is located within a customs station or is currently traveling towards one.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is empowered to depute other officers of customs to board a conveyance and determines the required duration for those officers to remain on board.
Officer of Customs: These officers may be deputed by an appropriate officer to board a conveyance and must remain on board for the duration deemed necessary by the appropriate officer.
Customs Station: The power to board a conveyance applies when the vessel or vehicle is located at or moving towards a customs-station.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Officer to be received and accommodation to be provided
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 61. Officer to be received and accommodation to be provided.- Whenever an officer of customs is so deputed to be on board any conveyance, the person-in-charge shall be bound to receive him on board and to provide him with suitable accommodation and adequate quantity of fresh water.

Officer of Customs: When an officer of customs is assigned to be on board a conveyance, they must be received by the person in charge.
The officer is entitled to receive suitable accommodation and an adequate supply of fresh water while on board.
Conveyance: A conveyance must accommodate assigned customs officers and provide them with fresh water when they are deputed to be on board.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance is legally bound to receive assigned customs officers and ensure they are provided with suitable accommodation and fresh water.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Officers' powers of access, etc
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
62. Officers' powers of access, etc.- (1) Every officer deputed as aforesaid shall have free access to every part of the conveyance and may-
(a) cause any goods to be marked before they are unloaded from that conveyance;
(b) lock up, seal, mark or otherwise secure any goods carried in the conveyance or any place or container in which they are carried; or
(c) fasten down any hatchway or entrance to the hold.
(2) If any box, place or closed receptacle in any such conveyance be locked, and the key be withheld, such officer shall report the same to the appropriate officer, who may thereupon issue to the officer on board the conveyance or to any other officer under his authority, a written order for search.
(3) On production of such order, the officer empowered thereunder may require that any such box, place or closed receptacle be opened in his presence; and if it be not opened upon his requisition, he may break open the same.

Officer of Customs: These officers are granted the authority to access any part of a conveyance for the performance of their duties.
They are empowered to mark, lock, seal, or secure goods and containers, and to fasten hatchways or entrances to holds to ensure compliance.
Conveyance: A conveyance is subject to the authority of customs officers who have the power to access its various parts and secure cargo or entry points.
When keys to locked areas or receptacles on a conveyance are withheld, customs officers may obtain and execute written search orders to force access if necessary.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer acts as the authorizing authority who receives reports regarding locked receptacles on a conveyance and may issue written orders for their search.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Sealing of conveyance
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 63. Sealing of conveyance.- Conveyances carrying transit goods for destinations outside 1[Bangladesh] or goods from some foreign territory to a customs-station or from a customs-station to some foreign territory may be sealed in such cases and in such manner as may be provided in the rules.

Conveyance: A conveyance used to transport transit goods to foreign destinations or goods between a customs station and foreign territory may be subject to sealing requirements as prescribed by the rules.
Transit Goods: Transit goods being transported through or from the country may be subject to sealing protocols on the conveyance for the protection of customs revenue and transit security.
Customs Station: Customs stations serve as authorized points for the arrival and departure of goods moving to or from foreign territories, where vessels carrying such goods may be subject to sealing procedures.
Rules: The rules provide the specific conditions and methods under which a conveyance may be sealed to ensure the integrity of goods in transit.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Goods not to be loaded or unloaded or water-borne except in presence of officer
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 64. Goods not to be loaded or unloaded or water-borne except in presence of officer.- Save where general permission is given under section 67 or with permission in writing of the appropriate officer, no goods other than passengers’ baggage or ballast urgently required to be loaded for the vessel's safety, shall be shipped or water-borne to be shipped or discharged from any vessel, in any customs-port, nor any goods except passenger’ baggage shall be loaded in or unloaded from any conveyance other than a vessel at any land customs-station or customs-airport except in the presence of an officer of customs.

Goods: The loading, unloading, or movement of goods for shipment is generally prohibited in customs-ports, land customs-stations, or customs-airports unless conducted in the presence of an officer of customs.
Exceptions to this requirement include passenger baggage and ballast that is urgently needed for the safety of a vessel.
Officer of Customs: The presence of an officer of customs is mandatory for the loading or unloading of goods at customs-ports, land customs-stations, and customs-airports, unless specific written permission is granted by an appropriate officer or general permission is provided under the relevant section of the Act.
Vessel: The loading or discharging of goods from any vessel in a customs-port must occur in the presence of an officer of customs, except when goods consist of passenger baggage or safety-critical ballast.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is empowered to grant written permission for the loading or unloading of goods in circumstances where the general presence of a customs officer is otherwise required.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Goods not to be loaded or unloaded or passed on certain days or at certain times
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
65. Goods not to be loaded or unloaded or passed on certain days or at certain times.- Except with the permission of the appropriate officer and on payment of such fees as may be prescribed by the Board no goods, other than passengers’ baggage or mail bags, shall in any customs-port be discharged, or be shipped or water-borne to be shipped or shall be loaded or unloaded or passed at any land customs-station or customs-airport-
(a) on any public holiday within the meaning of the section 25 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 (XXVI of 1881) or on any day on which the discharge or shipping of cargo at customs-port or loading, unloading, passage or delivery of cargo at any land customs-station or customs-airport, as the case may be, is prohibited by the Board by notification in the official Gazette; or
(b) on any day except between such hours as the Board may, from time to time, by like notification, appoint.

Appropriate Officer of Customs: The loading, unloading, or passage of goods outside of permitted times and days requires the specific permission of the appropriate officer of customs.
Goods: Except for passengers' baggage and mail bags, the loading, unloading, or passage of goods is restricted at customs ports, land customs stations, and customs airports during public holidays or times not appointed by the Board.
Passenger Baggage: Passenger baggage is excluded from the general restrictions on loading, unloading, and passage of goods during restricted days or hours.
Mail Bags: Mail bags are excluded from the general restrictions on loading, unloading, and passage of goods during restricted days or hours.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to prescribe fees for loading or unloading activities during restricted times and to issue notifications in the official Gazette prohibiting such activities on specific days or limiting them to certain hours.
Negotiable Instruments Act 1881: This Act provides the legal definition of public holidays, which serves as a criteria for determining restricted days for customs operations.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Goods not to be loaded or unloaded except at approved places
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 66. Goods not to be loaded or unloaded except at approved places.- Save where general permission is given under section 67 or with permission in writing of the appropriate officer, no imported goods shall be unloaded or goods for export loaded at any place other than a place duly approved under clause (b) of section 10 for the unloading or loading of such goods.

Imported Goods: Imported goods must not be unloaded at any location other than one that has been officially approved for such activities.
Export Goods: Goods intended for export must only be loaded at a place that has been duly approved for this purpose.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer of customs has the authority to grant written permission for the loading or unloading of goods at locations other than those officially approved.
Customs Procedure for Loading Goods: Loading and unloading activities are restricted to approved places unless a general permission is granted under section 67 or specific written permission is obtained from the appropriate officer.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to exempt from sections 64 and 66
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 67. Power to exempt from sections 64 and 66.- Notwithstanding anything contained in section 64 or section 66, the Board may, by notification in the official Gazette, give general permission for goods to be loaded at any customs-station from any place not duly appointed for loading and without the presence or authority of an officer of customs.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is empowered to issue notifications in the official Gazette granting general exemptions from the requirements set forth in sections 64 and 66 of the Customs Act.
Customs Station: The Board may authorize the loading of goods at a customs-station from locations not specifically appointed for such purposes, and without the presence or supervision of a customs officer.
Officer of Customs: The Board has the authority to permit the loading of goods at a customs-station without the presence or prior approval of an officer of customs.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Boat-note
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
68. Boat-note.- (1) When any goods are water-borne for the purpose of being landed from any vessel and warehoused or cleared for home-consumption, or of being shipped for exportation on board any vessel, there shall be sent, with each boat-load or other separate despatch, a boat-note specifying the number of packages so sent and the marks or number or other description thereof.
(2) Each boat-note for goods to be landed shall be signed by an officer of the vessel, and likewise by the officer of customs on board, if any such officer be on board, and shall be delivered on arrival to any officer of customs authorised to receive the same.
(3) Each boat-note for goods to be shipped shall be signed by the appropriate officer and, if an officer of customs is on board the vessel on which such goods are to be shipped, shall be delivered to such officer, and if no such officer be on board, shall be delivered to the master of the vessel or to an officer of the vessel appointed by him to receive it.
(4) The officer of customs who receives any boat-note of goods landed, and the officer of customs, master or other officer as the case may be, who receives any boat-note of goods shipped, shall sign the same and note thereon such particulars as the 1[Commissioner of Customs] may from time to time direct.
(5) The Board may from time to time, by notification in the official Gazette, suspend the operation of this section in any customs-port or part thereof.

Boat Note: A boat note is a mandatory document required for every dispatch of goods being moved by boat between a vessel and the shore, whether for landing or for exportation.
It must specify the quantity of packages, their marks, numbers, or other descriptions to identify the goods being transported.
The note requires specific signatures from vessel officers and customs officials depending on whether the goods are being landed or shipped for export.
Receiving officers must sign the boat note upon delivery and record additional particulars as directed by the Commissioner of Customs.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to issue directions regarding the specific particulars that must be noted on a boat note upon its receipt.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the legal authority to suspend the application of the boat note requirement in any customs-port or designated part thereof through an official gazette notification.
Customs Port: The Board may specify particular customs-ports or areas within them where the mandatory use of boat notes for goods movement is temporarily suspended.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Goods water-bone to be forthwith landed or shipped
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 69. Goods water-bone to be forthwith landed or shipped.- All goods water-borne for the purpose of being landed or shipped shall be landed or shipped without any unnecessary delay.

Goods: All goods that are water-borne for the purpose of landing or shipping must be processed without any unnecessary delay. This ensures the efficient movement of cargo during the loading or unloading process at a customs station.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Goods not to be transhipped without permission
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 70. Goods not to be transhipped without permission.- Except in cases of imminent danger, no goods discharged into or loaded in any boat for the purpose of being landed or shipped shall be transhipped into any other boat without the permission of an officer of customs.

Goods: Goods that have been discharged or loaded onto a boat for landing or shipping must not be moved to another boat without prior authorization, unless there is a situation of imminent danger.
Officer of Customs: The permission of an officer of customs is mandatory for the transhipment of goods between boats, except in circumstances involving immediate danger.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to prohibit plying of unlicensed cargo-boats
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
71. Power to prohibit plying of unlicensed cargo-boats.- (1) The Board may declare with regard to any customs-port, by notification in the official Gazette, that, after a date therein specified, no boat not duly licensed and registered shall be allowed to ply as a cargo-boat for the landing and shipping of merchandise within the limits of such port.
(2) In any port with regard to which such notification has been issued, the 1[Commissioner of Customs] or other officer whom the Board appoints in this behalf, may, subject to rules and on payment of such fees as the Board may, by notification in the official Gazette, prescribe, issue licences for and register cargo-boats, or cancel the same.

National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to declare through an official Gazette notification that unlicensed cargo-boats are prohibited from operating within the limits of a customs-port after a specified date.

The Board is empowered to authorize the Commissioner of Customs or another appointed officer to issue or cancel licenses for cargo-boats and to prescribe the fees payable for such licensing and registration.
Cargo Boat: Cargo-boats must be duly licensed and registered to operate for the landing and shipping of merchandise within designated customs-port limits after a notification is issued by the Board.
The licensing and registration of these boats are subject to rules and the payment of fees prescribed by the Board.
Customs Port: The Board may restrict the operation of cargo-boats within specific customs-ports by requiring mandatory licensing and registration for all vessels used for the landing and shipping of merchandise.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs, or another officer appointed by the Board, is authorized to issue and register licenses for cargo-boats or cancel such licenses in ports where the relevant notification is in force.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Plying of ships of less than one hundred tons
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
72. Plying of ships of less than one hundred tons.- (1) Every boat belonging to a 2[Bangladeshi] ship and every other vessel not exceeding one hundred tons, shall be marked in such manner as may be prescribed by rules.
(2) Plying of all or any class or description of vessels of less than one hundred tons, whether in sea or inland waters, may be prohibited or regulated or restricted as to the purposes and limits of plying by rules.

Vessel Marking Requirement: Every boat belonging to a Bangladeshi ship and any vessel under one hundred tons must be marked in a manner specified by rules.
Vessel Movement Regulation: The government may prohibit, regulate, or restrict the movement, purpose, and operational limits of vessels under one hundred tons in sea or inland waters through rules.

processed_clauses.metadata_title: CHAPTER IX - DISCHARGE OF CARGO AND ENTRY INWARDS OF GOODS
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
CHAPTER IX
DISCHARGE OF CARGO AND ENTRY INWARDS OF GOODS

Customs Cargo Handling: This chapter governs the procedures and regulations regarding the discharge of cargo from vessels at customs stations.
It outlines the foundational requirements for the official entry of goods into the jurisdiction under the Customs Act 1969.
Goods: This chapter establishes the legal framework for the arrival and processing of goods at a customs station.
It mandates specific protocols for the entry inwards of goods to ensure proper customs oversight and regulation.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Discharge of cargo by vessels may commence on receipt of due permission
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 73. Discharge of cargo by vessels may commence on receipt of due permission.- When an order for entry inwards of any vessel which has arrived in any customs-port or a special pass permeating such vessel to break bulk has been given, discharge of the cargo of such vessel may be proceeded with.

Vessel: A vessel must receive an order for entry inwards or a special pass before it is permitted to begin the discharge of cargo at a customs-port.
Customs Port: This is the designated location where a vessel must have formal authorization to break bulk and commence the discharge of its cargo.
Customs Cargo Handling: The discharge of cargo from a vessel is legally contingent upon the prior receipt of due permission or a special pass to break bulk.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Discharge of goods by conveyances other than vessels
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 74. Discharge of goods by conveyances other than vessels.- When on arrival of a conveyance other than a vessel at a land customs-station or customs- airport the person-in-charge of such conveyance has delivered the import manifest under section 44 and the documents required under section 48, he shall forthwith take the conveyance or cause it to be taken to the examination station at the land customs-station or customs-airport and remove or cause to be removed all goods carried in such conveyance to the custom-house in the presence of the appropriate officer or some person duly authorised by him in that behalf.

Conveyance: Upon arrival at a customs station or customs airport, the person in charge must move the conveyance to the designated examination station after fulfilling initial manifest and documentation requirements.
Customs Station: The person in charge of a conveyance is required to take the vehicle to the examination station located at the customs station for the purpose of discharging goods.
Customs Airport: Upon arrival, the person in charge must proceed to the examination station at the customs airport to facilitate the removal and discharge of goods.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: Following the delivery of the import manifest and required documents, this person must ensure the conveyance is moved to the examination station and that all goods are transferred to the custom house under official supervision.
Import Manifest: The delivery of this document is a mandatory prerequisite for the person in charge to proceed with the movement of the conveyance and the discharge of goods.
Customs Documents: The person in charge must submit all required documents under the relevant section of the Customs Act 1969 before initiating the discharge of goods.
Customs House: Goods carried by a conveyance must be removed and transported to this location in the presence of an appropriate officer or an authorized person.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The removal of goods from a conveyance to the custom house must be conducted in the presence of this officer or a person duly authorized by them.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Imported goods not to be unloaded unless entered in the import manifest
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
75. Imported goods not to be unloaded unless entered in the import manifest.- (1) No imported goods required to be shown in the import manifest shall, except with the permission of the appropriate officer, be unloaded from any conveyance at any customs-station unless they are specified in the import manifest or amended or supplementary import manifest for being unloaded at that customs-station.
(2) Nothing in the section shall apply to the unloading of the baggage accompanying a passenger or a member or a crew or mail bags.

Imported Goods: Imported goods that are required to be declared in an import manifest cannot be unloaded from a conveyance at a customs-station unless they are explicitly listed in the import manifest or its approved amendments.
Unloading of these goods without being specified in the manifest is prohibited unless the appropriate officer of customs grants specific permission.
Import Manifest: The import manifest serves as the legal record that must specify the goods intended to be unloaded at a customs-station.
Provisions allow for the submission of amended or supplementary import manifests to include goods for unloading.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer of customs holds the authority to grant permission for the unloading of imported goods that might otherwise not be permitted to be unloaded.
Conveyance: The unloading of imported goods from any conveyance at a customs-station is strictly regulated to ensure all items are entered in the import manifest.
Customs Station: The regulations concerning the mandatory inclusion of goods in an import manifest apply to all unloading activities occurring at a customs-station.
Baggage: The requirement to list goods in an import manifest before unloading does not apply to the baggage accompanying a passenger or a member of the crew.
Mail Bags: Mail bags are exempt from the requirement to be entered in the import manifest before they are unloaded at a customs-station.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Procedure in respect of goods not unloaded by vessels within time allowed
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
76. Procedure in respect of goods not unloaded by vessels within time allowed.- (1) (a) If any goods imported by a vessel (except such as have been shown in the import manifest as not to be unloaded) are not unloaded within such period as is specified in the bill of lading or if no period is so specified, within such number of the working days, not exceeding fifteen, after entry of the vessel as the Board may from time to time by notification in the official Gazette appoint, or
(b) if the cargo of any vessel, excepting a small quantity of goods, has been discharged before the expiration of the period so specified or appointed, the master of such vessel or, on this application, the appropriate officer may then carry such goods to the custom-house, there to remain for entry.
1[(2) The appropriate officer shall thereupon take charge of, and grant receipt for, such goods; and if notice in writing has been given by the master or the agent of the vessel to the appropriate officer that goods are to remain subject to a lien for freight, primage, general average demurrage, container detention charges, dead-freight, terminal handling charges, container service charge or other charges of a stated amount, the appropriate officer shall hold such goods until he receives notice in writing that the said charges have been paid.]

Imported Goods: These are goods imported by a vessel that remain unloaded after the time limit specified in the bill of lading or the period appointed by the Board.
The appropriate officer may move these goods to the custom-house for entry if they are not unloaded within the allowed timeframe, or if the majority of the cargo has been discharged early.
Vessel: The master of the vessel is responsible for ensuring goods are unloaded within the specified period or timeframe.
The master or agent may notify the appropriate officer that goods are subject to a lien for various outstanding charges, such as freight, demurrage, or container-related fees.
Bill of Lading: This document specifies the period within which imported goods must be unloaded from the vessel.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is authorized to notify, through the official Gazette, the maximum number of working days allowed for unloading goods after a vessel has entered.
Customs House: Goods that are not unloaded within the allowed time may be carried to the custom-house to be held until entry is processed.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is authorized to take charge of and issue a receipt for goods that have not been unloaded within the required time.
The officer must hold goods subject to a notified lien for freight and other listed charges until they receive written confirmation that these charges have been paid.
Agent: The agent of the vessel may provide written notice to the appropriate officer regarding liens on goods for unpaid charges, such as freight, demurrage, or terminal handling fees.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to land small parcels and hold unclaimed parcels
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
77. Power to land small parcels and hold unclaimed parcels.- (1) At any time after the arrival of any vessel, the appropriate officer may, with the consent of the master of such vessel, cause any small package or parcel of goods to be carried to the custom-house there to remain for entry in-charge of the officers of customs, during the remainder of the working days allowed under this Act for the landing of such package or parcel.
(2) In any package or parcel so carried to the custom-house remains unclaimed on the expiration of the number of working days so allowed for its unloading or at the time of the clearance outwards of the vessel from which it was unloaded, the master of such vessel may give such notice as is provided in section 76, and the officer-in-charge of the custom-house shall thereupon hold such package or parcel as provided in that section.

Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is empowered to arrange for the transfer of small packages or parcels from an arriving vessel to the custom-house with the consent of the vessel master.
Vessel: Upon arrival of a vessel, the appropriate officer may move small parcels or packages to the custom-house for entry.
Master of the Vessel: The master must provide consent for the removal of small parcels to the custom-house and is authorized to provide notice regarding unclaimed goods once the allowed unloading period or vessel clearance time has passed.
Customs House: The custom-house serves as the designated facility for holding small packages or parcels pending entry or further claim by the owner.
Officer of Customs: These officers are responsible for the custody of goods carried to the custom-house for the duration of the allowed working days.
Unclaimed Cargo: Parcels remaining at the custom-house after the allowed timeframe or upon the vessel's departure are subject to hold procedures as specified in the Act.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to permit immediate discharge
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
78. Power to permit immediate discharge.- (1) Notwithstanding anything contended in sections 74, 76 and 77, the appropriate officer in any customs-station to which the Board, by notification in the official Gazette, declares this section to apply, may permit the master of any vessel immediately on receipt of an order under section 47 or a special pass under section 49, or the person-in-charge of a conveyance other than a vessel on receipt of the import manifest to discharge the goods imported by such conveyance, or any portion thereof, into the custody of his agent, if he be willing to receive the same, for the purpose of unloading the same forthwith-
(a) at the custom-house, or at any specified landing-place or wharf; or
(b) at any landing-place or wharf belonging to the port commissioners, port trust, railways or other public body or company; or
(c) for giving it in the custody of such person as may be approved by the 2[Commissioner of Customs].
(2) Any agent so receiving such cargo or portion shall be bound to discharge all claims for damage or short delivery which may be established in respect of the same by the owner thereof, and shall be entitled to recover from such owner his charges for service rendered, but not for commission or the like, where any agent for the unloading of such cargo or portion has been previously appointed by the owner and such appointment is unrevoked 1[:
Provide that no agent so receiving such cargo or portion shall cause it to be removed or otherwise dealt with except in accordance with the written order of the appropriate officer.]
(3) The appropriate officer shall take charge of all goods discharged under clause (a) of sub-section (1) and otherwise proceed in relation thereto as provided in section 76 and 82.
(4) 2[A public body or company or port authority or airlines or] person at whose landing- place or wharf or place of storage any goods are discharged under clause (b) or clause (c) of sub-section (1) shall not permit the same to be removed or otherwise dealt with except in accordance with the order in writing of the appropriate officer.

Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer has the authority to permit the immediate discharge of goods from a vessel or conveyance into the custody of an agent, provided the customs-station has been declared applicable for this section by the Board.

This officer is responsible for managing the custody of goods discharged at custom-houses and ensuring that goods discharged at authorized landing places or warehouses are not removed or dealt with without written authorization.
The officer must proceed with the handling of discharged goods in accordance with the prescribed sections of the Customs Act 1969.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the power to designate specific customs-stations where the provision for immediate discharge of goods may be applied through a notification in the official Gazette.
Master of the Vessel: The master of a vessel may be permitted to immediately discharge imported goods upon receiving a valid arrival order or a special pass.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance other than a vessel is authorized to discharge imported goods upon receipt of the import manifest, subject to the permission of the appropriate officer.
Agent: An agent may receive imported goods for immediate discharge if they are willing to do so, assuming legal responsibility for claims related to damage or short delivery.

The agent is entitled to recover service charges from the owner of the goods but is prohibited from removing or dealing with the cargo except as permitted by the written order of the appropriate officer.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is authorized to approve the specific persons permitted to hold goods in custody under the immediate discharge provisions.
Port Authority: Port authorities, public bodies, or companies providing landing places or storage are prohibited from allowing the removal or handling of discharged goods without the written order of the appropriate officer.
Imported Goods: Imported goods may be discharged immediately into the custody of an agent at approved locations such as custom-houses, wharves, or other public body storage facilities to facilitate prompt unloading.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Entry for home-consumption or warehousing
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
79. Entry for home-consumption or warehousing.- (1) The owner of any imported goods shall make entry of such goods for home-consumption or warehousing or for any other approved purpose by delivering to the appropriate officer a bill of entry thereof in such form and manner and containing such particulars as the Board may direct:
Provided that, if the owner makes and subscribes a declaration before the appropriate officer to the effect that he is unable, for want of 3[such information as is essential for submitting a bill of entry], then the said officer shall permit him, previous to the entry thereof, to examine the goods in the presence of an officer of customs or to deposit such goods in a public warehouse appointed under section 12 without warehousing the same, pending the production of such information.
4[(1A) The Commissioner of Customs may within the period specified in sub-section (2) require the owner who has delivered or transmitted a bill of entry in electronic form to submit to the appropriate officer a paper bill of entry duly signed by the owner or his authorized agent, containing such information and documents as the said Commissioner may specify;]
5[(2) A bill of entry under sub-section (1) may be presented and the goods be cleared at any time within 20[thirty] days of the date of unloading thereof at a customs-port or a land customs-station or customs-inland container depot or 21[within twenty one days of] the date of unloading thereof at a customs- airport or within such extended period as the 6[Commissioner of Customs] may deem fit:
7[Provided that the Commissioner of Customs may permit a bill of entry to be presented even before the delivery of the manifest if the vessel or the aircraft by which the goods have been shipped for importation into Bangladesh is expected to arrive within thirty days from the date of such presentation.]
(3) If the 6[Commissioner of Customs] is satisfied that the rate of customs-duty is not adversely affected and that there was no intention to defraud, he may in exceptional circumstances and for reasons to be recorded in writing permit substitution of a bill of entry for home-consumption for a bill of entry for warehousing or vice versa.

Imported Goods: The owner of imported goods is required to submit a bill of entry for the purposes of home-consumption, warehousing, or other approved purposes.

In cases where essential information for a bill of entry is missing, the owner may be permitted to examine the goods or deposit them in a public warehouse pending the submission of the required details.
Bill of Entry: A bill of entry must be presented to the appropriate officer in a form and manner directed by the National Board of Revenue.
Electronic bills of entry may be subject to a request from the Commissioner of Customs for a signed paper version containing specific supporting information and documents.

The bill of entry generally must be presented within a specified timeframe following the unloading of goods at a customs-port, land customs-station, customs-inland container depot, or customs-airport, though extensions may be granted.
Under certain conditions, the Commissioner of Customs may allow a bill of entry to be presented prior to the delivery of the manifest.

A substitution between a bill of entry for home-consumption and one for warehousing may be permitted by the Commissioner of Customs in exceptional circumstances if there is no intention to defraud and customs-duty rates are not negatively impacted.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is responsible for receiving the bill of entry and supervising the examination of goods when necessary.
The appropriate officer may permit the deposit of goods into a public warehouse if the owner lacks the information required for a full entry.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to direct the form, manner, and required particulars for the submission of a bill of entry.
Public Warehouse: Goods may be deposited in a public warehouse pending the availability of information required for a formal bill of entry.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner has the authority to request a paper version of an electronic bill of entry and grant extensions for the presentation of such documents.
The Commissioner may permit the presentation of a bill of entry before the delivery of a manifest if the vessel or aircraft is expected to arrive within a defined period.

The Commissioner may authorize the substitution of a bill of entry for home-consumption with one for warehousing, or vice versa, provided specific conditions regarding duty rates and intent are satisfied.
Authorized Representative: An authorized agent may be required to sign and submit a paper bill of entry on behalf of the owner when requested by the Commissioner of Customs.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Acceptance of electronically transmitted bills of entry and documents
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 79A. Acceptance of electronically transmitted bills of entry and documents.- The Board may, by notification in the official Gazette, declare that electronically transmitted bills of entry and related documents may be acceptable subject to such conditions as are specified in that notification.

National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to authorize the acceptance of electronically transmitted bills of entry and related documents through a notification published in the official Gazette.
The Board retains the authority to prescribe specific conditions under which these electronic documents will be considered acceptable.
Bill of Entry: Electronically transmitted bills of entry are recognized as valid, provided they comply with the conditions specified by the Board in an official notification.
Customs Documents: Related customs documents transmitted electronically are accepted as valid subject to the conditions established by the Board in the official Gazette.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Access to Customs computer systems
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 79B. Access to 3[Customs computer] systems.- No person shall transmit to, or receive information from, a 3[Customs computer] system unless that person is registered by the Commissioner of Customs as a user of that 3[Customs computer] system.

Customs Computerised System: The transmission of information to or from the customs computer system is restricted to ensure only authorized interaction with the digital customs infrastructure.
Access to this system is contingent upon the formal registration of a person as a valid user by the relevant authority.
Commissioner of Customs: This official is empowered to register persons as users, thereby granting them the legal authority to transmit or receive information through the customs computerised system.
Registered User: Only individuals who have been formally registered by the Commissioner of Customs are permitted to interact with the customs computerised system.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Registered users
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
79C. Registered users.- (1) A person who wishes to be registered as a user of a 3[Customs computer] system may apply in writing to the Commissioner of Customs in the prescribed form and shall provide such information in relation to the application as required by the Commissioner.
(2) The said Commissioner may require an applicant for registration to give such additional information as the said Commissioner considers necessary for the purpose of the application.
(3) The said Commissioner may-
(a) grant the application subject to such conditions and limitations as the said Commissioner thinks fit; or
(b) refuse the application.
(4) The said Commissioner shall give notice in writing to the applicant of his decision.

Registered User: A person seeking to become a registered user of a customs computer system must submit an application to the Commissioner of Customs.

The application process requires the submission of information in a prescribed format, and applicants may be requested to provide additional details as deemed necessary by the Commissioner of Customs.
Customs Computerised System: This system allows for the registration of users who wish to access customs-related digital processes.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to process, approve, or refuse applications for user registration, and may impose specific conditions or limitations on such registration.
The Commissioner is responsible for notifying the applicant of the final decision regarding their registration request in writing.
Application Form: Applicants are required to submit their request for registration using the prescribed application form.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Registered users to be allocated unique user identifier
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
79D. Registered users to be allocated unique user identifier.- (1) A person who is registered as a user of a 3[Customs computer] system shall be allocated a unique user identifier for use in relation to that 3[Customs computer] system by the Commissioner of Customs, in such form or of such a nature as the Commissioner of Customs may determine.
(2) The unique user identifier allocated pursuant to sub-section (1) of this section shall be used by the registered user for the purpose of transmitting information to or receiving information from that 3[Customs computer] system.

Registered User: A person registered to use the customs computer system must be allocated a unique user identifier by the Commissioner of Customs.
The registered user is required to use the unique user identifier when transmitting information to or receiving information from the customs computer system.
Customs Computerised System: This system serves as the digital infrastructure for transmitting and receiving information between users and customs authorities.
Unique User Identifier: This is an identifier allocated to a registered user in a form or nature determined by the Commissioner of Customs for the purpose of interacting with the customs computer system.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is empowered to determine the form and nature of the unique user identifier and is responsible for its allocation to registered users.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Use of unique user identifier
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
79E. Use of unique user identifier.- (1) Where information is transmitted to a 3[Customs computer] system using a unique user identifier issued to a registered user by the Commissioner of Customs for that purpose, the transmission of that information shall, in the absence of proof to the contrary, be sufficient evidence that the registered user to whom the unique user identifier has been issued has transmitted that information.
(2) Where a unique user identifier is used by an individual who is not entitled to use it, sub-section (1) of this section does not apply if the registered user to whom the unique user identifier was issued has, prior to the unauthorized use of the unique user identifier, notified the Commissioner of Customs in writing that the unique user identifier is no longer secure.

Unique User Identifier: A unique user identifier is issued by the Commissioner of Customs to a registered user for the purpose of transmitting information to the customs computer system.
The use of a unique user identifier in a transmission is deemed to be evidence that the registered user transmitted the information, unless proven otherwise.

Registered users are protected from the legal consequences of unauthorized use of their unique user identifier if they have notified the Commissioner of Customs in writing that the identifier is no longer secure.
Customs Computerised System: This system serves as the infrastructure for the electronic transmission of customs-related information.
Registered User: A registered user is an individual or entity authorized to use a unique user identifier for submitting information to the customs system.
The registered user bears legal responsibility for transmissions made under their identifier unless they have reported the identifier as insecure prior to an unauthorized event.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is responsible for issuing unique user identifiers to registered users.
The Commissioner of Customs receives written notification from registered users in instances where a unique user identifier is no longer secure.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Cancellation of registration of registered user
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
79F. Cancellation of registration of registered user.- (1) Where at any time the Commissioner of Customs having jurisdiction is satisfied that a person who is a registered user of a 1[Customs computer] system has-
(a) failed to comply with a condition of registration imposed by the said Commissioner under section 79C (3) of this Act; or
(b) failed to comply with, or acted in contravention of, any conditions imposed by the said Commissioner under section 79D(3) of this Act in relation to the use and security of the registered users unique user identifier; or
(c) has been convicted of an offence under this Act in relation to improper access to or interference with a 1[Customs computer] system,-
the said Commissioner may cancel the registration of that individual as a registered user by giving notice in writing to that person setting out the reasons for the cancellation.

Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to cancel the registration of a registered user if they determine that the user has failed to comply with registration conditions, breached security requirements for identifiers, or committed an offence related to the customs computer system.
The Commissioner is required to provide written notice to the registered user explaining the reasons for the cancellation of their registration.
Registered User: A registered user of a customs computer system may have their registration cancelled by the Commissioner of Customs for failures related to regulatory compliance, improper use of unique identifiers, or conviction for offences involving the customs computer system.
Customs Computerised System: The registration of users who access the customs computer system is subject to specific regulatory conditions and security requirements enforced by the Commissioner of Customs.
Offences involving improper access to or interference with the customs computer system serve as grounds for the cancellation of a user's registration.
Unique User Identifier: Registered users are required to comply with conditions imposed by the Commissioner regarding the security and use of their unique user identifier, and failure to do so may lead to the cancellation of their registration.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Customs to keep records of transmission
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
79G. Customs to keep records of transmission.- (1) The Customs must keep a record of every transmission sent to or received from a registered user using a 1[Customs computer] system.
(2) The record described in sub-section (1) of this section must be kept for a period of five years from the date of the sending of or the receipt of the transmission, or for such other period as may be prescribed.

Customs Computerised System: The customs authority is required to maintain a comprehensive record of all data transmissions sent to or received from a registered user through the customs computerized system.
Registered User: A registered user is an authorized party whose digital communications with the customs authority must be documented and preserved by the customs department.
Customs Records Retention: Records of digital transmissions must be retained for a mandatory period of five years following the date of the communication.
The retention period may alternatively be specified as a different duration if prescribed by law or regulation.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Assessment of duty
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
80. Assessment of duty.- (1) On the delivery 2[or electronic transmission] of such bill, the goods or such part thereof as may be necessary may, without undue delay, be examined or tasted 3[in the presence of the owner or his agent, unless due to any exceptional circumstance such presence cannot be allowed,] and thereafter the goods shall be assessed to duty, if any, and the owner of such goods may then proceed to clear the same for home-consumption or warehouse them, subject to the provisions hereinafter contained.
(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1), imported goods prior to examination or testing thereof may be permitted by the appropriate officer to be assessed to duty on the basis of the statements made in the bill relating thereto and the information furnished under the rules and the documents produced under section 26; but if it is found subsequently on examination or testing of the goods or otherwise that any statement in such bill or document or any information so furnished is not correct in respect of any matter relating to the assessment, the goods shall, without prejudice to any other action which may be taken under this Act, be re-assessed to duty.
4[(3) The Board may by notification in the official gazette, exempt in the public interest any goods or class of goods imported by an importer or a class of importer from the requirement of examination and testing of the goods under sub-section (1).
(4) Upon delivery or transmission of the bill of entry for the goods exempted under sub-section (3) the duty shall be deemed to have been duly assessed for the purposes of this section:
Provided that where the appropriate officer has reason to believe that in case of any bill of entry re-assessment is necessary, he may, by recording reasons in writing, re-assess the duty payable for the goods and take such other actions as he may deem fit under this Act.]

Bill of Entry: The submission or electronic transmission of a bill of entry initiates the process for goods examination and subsequent assessment of duty.
Goods exempted from examination under specific official notifications are deemed to be duly assessed upon the delivery or transmission of the bill of entry.
An appropriate officer may mandate a re-assessment of duty if they have recorded written reasons to believe the initial assessment of a bill of entry was incorrect.
Goods: Imported goods may be examined or tested in the presence of the owner or their agent, subject to exceptional circumstances, before being assessed for duty.
Goods may be cleared for home consumption or placed in a warehouse following their assessment for duty.
Goods may be subject to re-assessment if subsequent examination reveals that the original statements or information provided in documentation were incorrect.
Customs Assessment: Assessment of duty occurs after the examination or testing of goods, allowing the owner to proceed with clearance or warehousing.
Appropriate officers may permit assessment based on submitted statements and documentation prior to the physical examination of the goods.
Any errors identified in the initial assessment documentation necessitate a re-assessment of the goods without prejudice to other legal actions available under the Act.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is authorized to permit the assessment of goods based on submitted documentation before physical examination occurs.
The officer has the authority to conduct re-assessments of duty by recording written reasons if there is a belief that the initial assessment was inaccurate.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to issue official gazette notifications to exempt specific goods or classes of importers from mandatory examination and testing requirements.
Agent: The owner or their agent is permitted to be present during the examination or testing of goods, unless exceptional circumstances prevent such attendance.
Importer: Importers are responsible for ensuring the accuracy of statements and information provided in bills of entry and related documents, as errors may lead to mandatory re-assessment of duty.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Provisional assessment of duty
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
81. Provisional assessment of duty.- (1) Where it is not possible immediately to assess the customs-duty that may be payable on any imported goods entered for home-consumption or for warehousing or for clearance from a warehouse for home-consumption or on any goods entered for exportation, for the reason that the goods require chemical or other test 1[or a further enquiry] for purposes of assessment, or that all the documents or complete documents or full information pertaining to those goods have not been furnished, an officer not below the rank of 2[Assistant Commissioner of Customs] may order that the duty payable on such goods be assessed provisionally:
Provided that the importer (same in the case of goods entered for warehousing) or the exporter pays such additional amount as security or furnishes such guarantee of a scheduled bank for the payment thereof as the said officer deems sufficient to meet the excess of the final assessment of duty over the provisional assessment.
[(2) Where any goods are allowed to be cleared or delivered on the basis of such provisional assessment, the amount of duty actually payable on those goods shall, within a period of one hundred and twenty working days from the date of the provisional assessment, where there is a case pending at any court, tribunal or appellate authority, from the date of receipt of the final disposal order of that case, be finally assessed and on completion of such assessment the appropriate officer shall order that the amount already guaranteed be adjusted against the amount payable on the basis of final assessment, and the difference between them shall be paid forthwith to or by the importer or exporter as the case may be:
Provided that the Board may, under exceptional circumstances recorded in writing, extend the period of final assessment specified under this sub-section.]

Provisional Assessment of Customs Duty: This mechanism allows for the assessment of duty on imported or exported goods when immediate final assessment is not possible due to the need for testing, further enquiry, or incomplete documentation.

The officer, who must be at least of the rank of an Assistant Commissioner of Customs, may authorize this process provided that adequate security or a scheduled bank guarantee is furnished to cover any potential excess duty determined upon final assessment.
Assistant Commissioner of Customs: This officer is the minimum authority empowered to order the provisional assessment of duty for goods entered for home consumption, warehousing, or exportation.
Imported or Exported Goods: Goods subject to provisional assessment require either chemical testing, other types of analysis, or additional information and documentation before their final duty liability can be determined.
Scheduled Bank: A guarantee from a scheduled bank may be furnished by the importer or exporter as security for the payment of duty pending the finalization of the assessment.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to extend the statutory time limit for final assessment under exceptional circumstances that must be recorded in writing.
Importer: The importer is responsible for providing the necessary security or bank guarantee to cover duty payments and is liable to pay or receive the difference once the final assessment is completed.
Exporter: The exporter is required to provide the necessary security or bank guarantee for provisional assessment cases and must settle any difference between the provisionally paid amount and the final assessed duty.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Procedure in case of goods not cleared or warehoused or transhipped after unloading within a specified period
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
82. Procedure in case of goods not cleared or warehoused or transhipped after unloading within a specified period.- 6[(1)] If any goods are not entered and cleared for home-consumption or warehoused or transhipped within 22[thirty] days of the date of unloading thereof at a customs-port or a land customs-station 23[or customs-inland container depot], or within 24[twenty one] days of the date of unloading thereof at a customs-airport or within such extended period as the appropriate officer may allow, such goods may, after due notice given to the owner, if his address could be ascertained, or published in the newspaper, if his address could not be ascertained, be sold under the orders of the appropriate officer:
Provided that -
(a) animals and perishable and hazardous goods may, with the permission of the appropriate officer, be sold at any time;
(b) arms, ammunition or military stores may be sold or otherwise disposed of at such time and place and in such manner as the Board may, with the approval of the Government, direct:
Provided further that nothing in this section shall authorise removal for home-consumption of any dutiable goods without payment of customs-duties thereon.]
1[(2) Where any goods are sold under sub-section (1) pending adjudication, appeal, revision or decision of a court, the proceeds of such sale shall be deposited into the Government treasury; and, if on such adjudication or in such appeal or revision it is found or if the court finds that the goods so sold are not liable to confiscation, the proceeds of the sale shall, after necessary deduction of dues, taxes or duties as provided in section 201, be refunded to the owner.]

Goods: If goods are not cleared, warehoused, or transhipped within the prescribed time limits after unloading, the appropriate customs officer may initiate sale proceedings.
The sale process requires providing notice to the owner either directly or through a newspaper publication.
Customs Port: This location acts as a point of entry where the time limit for clearing, warehousing, or transhipping goods is defined.
Land Customs Station: This location serves as a point of entry where specific time frames apply for the clearing, warehousing, or transhipping of goods.
Customs-inland container depot: This facility is designated as a point of entry subject to the same time-bound clearance, warehousing, and transhipment procedures as other customs stations.
Customs Airport: This facility has a distinct, shorter timeframe for the clearing, warehousing, or transhipping of unloaded goods compared to ports and land stations.
Perishable and Hazardous Goods: These specific categories of goods may be sold at any time prior to the expiry of standard waiting periods, subject to the permission of the appropriate officer.
Arms and Ammunition: The disposal or sale of these items is strictly directed by the National Board of Revenue, with approval from the Government, rather than through standard auction procedures.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is authorized to allow extensions for the clearance of goods, oversee the sale of goods under this section, and grant permission for the early sale of perishable or hazardous items.
Sale Proceeds Disbursement: If goods are sold pending legal adjudication or appeal, the proceeds are held in the government treasury; if it is subsequently determined that the goods were not liable to confiscation, the net proceeds are refunded to the owner after deducting relevant duties and taxes.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to direct the time, place, and manner of the disposal of arms, ammunition, and military stores, subject to government approval.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Procedure in case of goods not assessed or out-passed by Customs after presentation of the related bill of entry within a specified period
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
82A. Procedure in case of goods not assessed or out-passed by Customs after presentation of the related bill of entry within a specified period.- If any goods, other than goods detained, seized, confiscated, under adjudication or appeal under the provisions of this Act, for which a bill of entry has duly been presented, are not assessed and out-passed within seven working days the owner of such goods may serve a notice upon the Commissioner to finalize the Customs formalities within three working days enabling him to pay duty and taxes and clear the goods, and the said Commissioner or any officer authorized on his behalf shall do so, if the import is in order, or issue a show cause notice if the import is not in order.
Explanation.- For the purpose of this section "detained goods" include goods detained for chemical examination, radiation test, reference for resolution disputes on of classification, value, ITC aspect or any other legal disputes.]

Bill of Entry: This entity represents the document presented to Customs for the clearance of imported goods.
The submission of a bill of entry initiates the customs assessment process and triggers the timeline for the finalization of customs formalities.
Detained Goods: These are goods held by customs authorities for specific reasons such as chemical examination, radiation testing, or disputes regarding classification, valuation, and import policy requirements.
Detained goods are explicitly excluded from the simplified procedure for clearance when assessment or out-passing is delayed beyond the specified time frame.
Seized Goods: These goods are excluded from the expedited clearance procedure applicable to goods awaiting assessment or out-passing.
Confiscated Goods: These goods are excluded from the expedited clearance procedure applicable to goods awaiting assessment or out-passing.
Adjudication of Customs Cases: Goods subject to pending adjudication under the provisions of the Customs Act are ineligible for the fast-track clearance notice process defined for delayed assessments.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs or an authorized officer is responsible for finalizing customs formalities within a set time frame upon receiving a notice from the goods owner.
If the import formalities are not in order, the Commissioner or authorized officer must issue a show cause notice to the importer.
Show Cause Notice: This legal instrument is issued by the Commissioner of Customs when the import documentation or status is found to be non-compliant or not in order.
Customs Clearance Procedure: A procedural framework is established to ensure goods are assessed and out-passed within a specific period after the submission of the bill of entry.
When delays occur, owners of goods may invoke a notice procedure to compel the customs authority to complete assessment or provide a formal explanation for non-compliance.

processed_clauses.metadata_title: CHAPTER X CLEARANCE OF GOODS FOR HOME-CONSUMPTION
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
CHAPTER X
CLEARANCE OF GOODS FOR HOME-CONSUMPTION

Customs Clearance: This chapter outlines the legal framework and procedures governing the clearance of goods for home consumption under the Customs Act 1969.
Goods: The provisions in this chapter regulate the specific legal requirements and conditions that must be fulfilled for goods to be cleared and released for home consumption within the country.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Clearance for home-consumption
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
83. Clearance for home-consumption.- 3[1] When the owner of any goods entered for home-consumption and assessed under section 80 has paid the import duty and other charges, if any in respect of the same, the appropriate officer, if he is satisfied that the import of the goods is not prohibited or in breach of any restrictions or conditions applying to the importer of such goods, may make an order for the clearance of the same.
3[(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) the importer or a class of importers for any goods, notified under section 80(3), shall be allowed clearance without any formal order under sub-section(1) of this section and such goods shall be deemed to have been duly allowed to pass.]
25[(3) The Board may, by special order, in the public interest, allow any government or semi-government organization or statutory public authority to take clearance of goods without paying the import duty and other charges on submission of a guarantee that such duty and charges shall be paid within specific period to be determined by the Board.]

Customs Clearance: The appropriate officer may authorize the clearance of goods for home-consumption once all applicable import duties and charges have been paid and the officer is satisfied that the importation complies with all legal restrictions.
Specific categories of importers notified under the law may be granted clearance without requiring a formal order, with such goods deemed to have been duly authorized for entry.

The National Board of Revenue has the authority to issue special orders allowing government or statutory bodies to clear goods without immediate payment of duties, provided a guarantee is submitted to ensure payment within a set timeframe.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is responsible for verifying the compliance of imported goods and issuing the formal clearance order once duties are settled and import conditions are met.
Importer: The importer is responsible for the payment of import duties and charges for goods entered for home-consumption.
Certain classes of importers may be exempted from the requirement of a formal clearance order for their goods as specified by law.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the power to permit government and statutory organizations to defer duty payments for imported goods through special orders in the public interest.
Import Duty: Import duties and other applicable charges must be paid by the owner of goods entered for home-consumption before a clearance order can be issued.
The Board may authorize exemptions or deferrals for specific public sector organizations under a guarantee scheme.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Amendment of assessment
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
83A. Amendment of assessment. - (1) An officer of Customs not below the rank of an Assistant Commissioner of Customs may from time to time make or cause to be made such amendments to an assessment of duty or to the value taken for the purpose of assessment of duty as he thinks necessary in order to ensure the correctness of the assessment even though the goods to which the value or the duty relates have already passed out of Customs control or the duty originally assessed has been paid.
(2) If the amendment has the effect of imposing a fresh liability or enhancing an existing liability, a demand notice in writing shall be given by the officer of Customs to the person liable for the duty.
(3) Unless otherwise specified in this Act, the due date for payment against the aforesaid demand notice shall be thirty working days from the date of issue of such a written demand notice by the officer of Customs.

Assistant Commissioner of Customs: This officer is empowered to initiate amendments to duty assessments or the value of goods used for such assessments to ensure accuracy, even after the goods have exited customs control or the initial duty has been paid.
Customs Assessment: Amendments to duty assessments may be made periodically to ensure the correctness of the final tax or value determination applied to goods.
Value: The value used for the purpose of assessing customs duty is subject to amendment by an authorized officer to maintain accuracy.
Customs Control: Amendments to a customs assessment may proceed even if the relevant goods have already passed out of customs control.
Duty Payment: In cases where an amendment results in a new or increased liability, a formal written demand notice must be served to the person liable for the duty.
The deadline for settling payments resulting from such a demand notice is thirty working days from the date the notice is issued, unless the Act specifies otherwise.
Person: A person becomes liable to pay additional duties or liabilities if an assessment amendment results in a fresh or enhanced financial obligation, for which a written notice will be issued.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Limitation of time for amendment assessments
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
83B. Limitation of time for amendment assessments.- (1) Where an assessment of duty has been made under this Act, the officer of Customs is not entitled to increase the amount of the assessment after the expiration of three years from the date on which the original assessment was made.
(2) Notwithstanding sub-section (1) of this section, in any case where the entry or any declaration made in relation to the goods was fraudulent or willfully misleading, the officer of Customs may amend the assessment at any time 26[***] so as to increase the amount of the assessment.

Customs Assessment: The assessment of duty under the Customs Act is subject to a time limitation, after which an officer of Customs cannot increase the assessed amount.

An amendment to increase an assessment is restricted to a period of three years from the date of the original assessment, unless the original entry or declaration was fraudulent or willfully misleading, in which case the assessment can be amended at any time.
Officer of Customs: This officer is responsible for conducting assessments of duty and is prohibited from increasing the assessment amount after a set statutory time limit.

In cases involving fraud or willful misrepresentation in a declaration or entry, the officer is empowered to amend an assessment to increase the duty amount without being bound by the standard three-year limitation.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal framework governing the assessment of customs duties and specifies the conditions and time limitations under which those assessments may be amended.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Audit or examination of records
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
83C. Audit or examination of records.- (1) An officer of Customs may at any time enter any premises or place where records are kept pursuant to section 211 of this Act and audit and examine those records either in relation to specific transactions or to the adequacy or integrity of the manual or electronic system or systems by which such records are created and stored.
(2) For the purposes of sub-section (1) of this section, an officer of Custom shall have full and free access to all lands, buildings and places and to all books, records and documents, whether in the custody or under the control of the licensee, importer, exporter or any other person, for the purpose of inspecting any books, records, and documents and any property, process, or matter that the officer considers.-
(a) necessary or relevant for the purpose of collecting any duty under the Act or for the purpose of carrying out any other function lawfully conferred on the officer, or
(b) likely to provide any information otherwise required for the purposes of this Act or for the discharge of any functions under this Act.
(3) The officer of Customs may make extracts from or copies of any such books, documents or records.
(4) Notwithstanding sub-section (2) and (3) of this section, an officer of Customs shall not enter any private dwelling except with the consent of an occupier or owner thereof or pursuant to a warrant issued under this Act.]

Customs Officer: A Customs Officer is authorized to enter premises where records are kept to audit and examine them in relation to specific transactions or the integrity of the systems used to store them.

A Customs Officer has the power to access lands, buildings, places, books, and documents held by any person to collect duty or perform functions under the Act, including making copies or extracts of such documents.
A Customs Officer is restricted from entering a private dwelling without the consent of the owner or occupier, or unless they have obtained a warrant issued under the Act.
Customs Records Retention: Records that are required to be kept under the Act are subject to audit and examination by an officer of Customs at any time.
Licensee: A licensee must grant the officer of Customs full and free access to their books, records, documents, and premises for the purpose of an audit or examination.
Importer: An importer must provide the officer of Customs with full and free access to their books, records, and documents to facilitate the audit and examination process as required by the Act.
Exporter: An exporter is subject to the authority of a Customs Officer who may examine their records and premises to ensure compliance with duty collection and other legal functions.
Search Warrant: A warrant is required if a Customs Officer intends to enter a private dwelling for the purposes of audit or examination without the consent of the occupant or owner.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to appoint auditor, etc.
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 83D. Power to appoint auditor, etc.- Board may, by issuance of special order, appoint, on such terms and conditions as it may deem appropriate, professional auditor or audit firm for carrying out audit on any Customs matter; and such auditor or audit firm shall be deemed to be an officer of Customs for the purpose of this section.]

National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to appoint professional auditors or audit firms to conduct audits on any customs-related matters.
The Board determines the terms and conditions for the engagement of such audit professionals.
Professional Auditor: A professional auditor or audit firm appointed under this provision is legally deemed to be an officer of Customs for the purposes of the audit mandate.
They are appointed by the Board under specific terms and conditions to perform audits on customs matters.
Customs Audit: The law provides a framework for the Board to commission specialized audits on customs matters to be conducted by appointed professional auditors or firms.
Officer of Customs: Professional auditors or audit firms, while performing authorized audit functions, are granted the status of an officer of Customs for the purposes of this section.

processed_clauses.metadata_title: CHAPTER XI WAREHOUSING
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
CHAPTER XI
WAREHOUSING

Warehousing Station: This chapter governs the legal framework and procedures for the establishment and operation of warehousing stations under the customs jurisdiction.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Application to warehouse
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 84. Application to warehouse.- When any dutiable goods have been entered for warehousing and assessed under section 80, the owner of such goods may apply for leave to deposit the same in any warehouse appointed or licensed under this Act.

Goods: Once dutiable goods have been entered for warehousing and duly assessed, the owner may request authorization to deposit them in an approved or licensed warehouse.
Warehouse: The law provides a framework for the deposit of assessed dutiable goods into any facility that has been officially appointed or licensed to act as a warehouse.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal authority for the appointment or licensing of warehouses where owners of assessed goods may apply to store their inventory.
Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of goods that have been assessed for warehousing is authorized to apply for permission to store those items in a licensed or appointed warehouse.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Form of application
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 85. Form of application.- Every such application shall be in writing signed by the applicant, and shall be in such form as may be prescribed by the Board.

Application Form: Applications must be submitted in writing and signed by the applicant.
The specific format of the application must be that which is prescribed by the National Board of Revenue.
