National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is empowered to prescribe the form that must be used for formal applications.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Warehousing bond
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
86. Warehousing bond.- (1) When any such application has been made in respect of any goods, the owner of the goods to which it relates shall execute a bond, binding himself in a penalty of twice the amount of the duty assessed under section 80 or section 81 1[* *] on such goods,-
(a) to observe all provisions of this Act and the rules in respect of such goods;
(b) to pay on or before a date specified in a notice of demand all duties, rent and charges payable in respect of such goods together with interest on the same from the date so specified at the rate 2[to be determined by the Board, being a rate not less than the bank rate fixed by the Bangladesh Bank and not more than double the Bank rate so fixed]; and
(c) to discharge all penalties incurred for violation of the provisions of this Act and the rules in respect of such goods.
(2) Every such bond shall be in such form as is from time to time prescribed by the Board, and shall relate to the goods or portion of goods of one conveyance only.
(3) Notwithstanding anything in sub-section (2), for the purposes of sub- section (1), the 3[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] may permit any importer to entry into a general bond in such amount and subject to such conditions, limitations or restrictions as the 3[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] may determine in respect of the warehousing of goods to be imported by such importer within a specified period.
(4) A bond executed under this section by an importer in respect of any goods shall continue in force notwithstanding the transfer of the goods to any other person or the removal of the goods to another warehouse or warehousing station:
Provided that, where the whole of the goods or any part thereof are transferred to another person, the appropriate officer may accept a fresh bond from the transferee in a sum equal to twice the amount of the duty assessed on the goods transferred and thereupon the bond executed by the transferer shall be deemed to be discharged to the extent to which the fresh bond has been executed by the transferee.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner is required to execute a bond upon making an application for warehousing, committing to a penalty of twice the assessed duty amount.
The owner must comply with all provisions of the Customs Act and relevant rules concerning the goods, including payment of duties, rent, charges, and applicable interest.
Bonded Warehouse: The warehouse operations are governed by a bond that covers goods imported by a single conveyance.
The bond remains in force even if goods are transferred to another person or moved to a different warehouse or warehousing station.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to determine the rate of interest applicable to unpaid duties and charges, ensuring it falls within a range defined by the prevailing bank rate set by the Bangladesh Bank.
The Board is responsible for prescribing the form to be used for warehousing bonds.
Commissioner of Customs: This officer, or any other Commissioner of Customs authorized by the Board, may permit an importer to enter into a general bond for warehousing goods imported within a specific period.
They have the authority to determine the conditions, limitations, or restrictions applicable to such general bonds.
Importer: Importers may be permitted to execute a general bond in lieu of individual bonds for warehousing goods, subject to the discretion and conditions set by the Commissioner of Customs (Bond).
A bond executed by an importer remains in effect despite the subsequent transfer of the goods to another party.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer may accept a fresh bond from a transferee when warehoused goods are sold or transferred to a new owner.
Upon the acceptance of a fresh bond from the transferee, the original bond executed by the transferor is deemed discharged to that extent.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal framework for the execution of warehousing bonds, the payment of duties and interest, and the enforcement of penalties for non-compliance.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Warehousing bank guarantee
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 86A. Warehousing bank guarantee.- Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act regarding execution of a bond in relation to clearance of goods for warehousing, the Board or a Commissioner of Customs authorised in this behalf by the Board, may, in addition to requiring execution of bond, direct that a bank guarantee, for an amount not exceeding the duties leviable on the goods, be furnished in such manner as may be prescribed.

Bonded Warehouse Goods: The authorities may require a bank guarantee in addition to a standard bond for the clearance of goods intended for warehousing.
The amount of the required bank guarantee must not exceed the total duties leviable on the goods.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to authorize a Commissioner of Customs to mandate the submission of a bank guarantee for warehousing goods.
The Board holds the authority to determine the prescribed manner for furnishing such bank guarantees.
Commissioner of Customs: When authorized by the Board, a Commissioner of Customs may direct an importer to furnish a bank guarantee in addition to the execution of a bond for warehousing.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Forwarding of goods to warehouse
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
87. Forwarding of goods to warehouse.- (1) When the provisions of section 85 and 86 have been complied with in respect of any goods, such goods shall be delivered to the owner of such goods or his authorized representative for onward transportation to the warehouse in which they are to be deposited.
(2) A pass shall be sent with the goods specifying the name of the owner of such goods and the name or number of the importing conveyance, the marks, numbers and contents of each package, and the warehouse or place in the warehouse wherein they are to be deposited.
(3) After depositing such goods mentioned in sub-section (1) the owner of such goods shall inform the concerned Commissioner of Customs regarding the warehousing of the goods.

Goods: After compliance with relevant sections, these goods are to be delivered to the owner or authorized representative for transport to a designated warehouse.
A pass must accompany the goods during transit, detailing specific package information and the intended warehouse destination.
Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner or their authorized representative is responsible for taking delivery of goods for transport to the warehouse.
Upon successful deposit of the goods in the warehouse, the owner must notify the appropriate Commissioner of Customs regarding the status of the warehousing.
Authorized Representative: The authorized representative is empowered to receive goods on behalf of the owner for the purpose of onward transportation to a warehouse.
Warehouse: This facility serves as the destination for goods being transported from customs control, with specific locations inside the warehouse identified in the accompanying pass.
Conveyance: The pass accompanying the goods must specify the name or number of the importing conveyance used to bring the goods into the customs jurisdiction.
Commissioner of Customs: The owner is required to inform the concerned Commissioner of Customs once the goods have been successfully deposited into the warehouse.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Receipt of goods at warehouse
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
88. Receipt of goods at warehouse.- (1) On receipt of the goods, the pass shall be examined by the warehouse-keeper, and shall be returned to the appropriate officer.
(2) No package, but, cask or other container shall be admitted into any warehouse unless it bears the marks and numbers specified in, and otherwise corresponds with, the pass for its admission.
(3) If the goods be found to correspond with the pass, the warehouse- keeper shall certify to that effect on the pass, and the warehousing of such goods shall be deemed to have been completed.
(4) If the goods do not so correspond, the fact shall be reported by the warehouse-keeper for the orders of the appropriate officer, and the goods shall either be returned to the custom-house in charge of an officer of customs or kept in deposit pending such orders as the warehouse-keeper deems most convenient.
(5) If the quantity or value of any goods has been incorrectly stated in the bill of entry, due to inadvertence or bona fide error, the error may be rectified at any time before the warehousing of the goods is completed, and not subsequently.

Warehouse Keeper: The warehouse keeper is responsible for examining the pass upon receipt of goods and returning it to the appropriate officer.
The warehouse keeper must verify that incoming packages or containers correspond to the specifications on the admission pass before admitting them into the warehouse.
When goods correspond to the pass, the warehouse keeper must certify this to complete the warehousing process.

In cases where goods do not correspond to the pass, the warehouse keeper must report the discrepancy to the appropriate officer and either return the goods to the custom-house or hold them in deposit.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer receives the pass back from the warehouse keeper after the examination of goods.
The appropriate officer provides orders regarding the handling of goods that do not match the specifications on their admission pass.
Goods: Goods must correspond to the marks and numbers listed on the admission pass to be admitted into a warehouse.
If goods do not match the admission pass, they must be reported by the warehouse keeper and either returned to the custom-house or held until instructions are received.

Errors regarding the quantity or value of goods stated in the bill of entry can be rectified if they were made inadvertently or due to a bona fide error, provided this happens before the warehousing is completed.
Warehouse: A warehouse only admits packages or containers that bear the marks and numbers specified in their admission pass.
Bill of Entry: Any incorrect statements regarding the quantity or value of goods within the bill of entry may be corrected only prior to the completion of the warehousing process.
Customs House: Goods that do not correspond to their admission pass may be returned to the custom-house in the custody of a customs officer.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Goods how warehoused
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 89. Goods how warehoused.- Except as provided in section 94, all goods shall be warehoused in the packages, butts, casks or other containers in which they have been imported.

Warehoused Goods: Goods must be stored in the same packages, containers, or receptacles in which they were originally imported, unless specified otherwise under the provisions of the Customs Act.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Warrant to be given when goods are warehoused
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
90. Warrant to be given when goods are warehoused.- (1) Whenever any goods are lodged in a public warehouse or a licensed private warehouse, the warehouse-keeper shall deliver a warrant signed by him as such to the person lodging the goods.
(2) Such warrant shall be in such form as the Board may from time to time prescribed, and shall be transferable by the endorsement; and the endorsee shall be entitled to receive the goods specified in such warrant on the same terms as those on which the person who originally lodged the goods would have been entitled to receive the same.
(3) The Board may, by notification in the official Gazette, exempt any class of goods from the operation of this section.

Public Warehouse: The warehouse-keeper must provide a signed warrant to the person lodging goods when they are stored in a public warehouse.
Private Warehouse: When goods are lodged in a licensed private warehouse, the warehouse-keeper is required to issue a signed warrant to the depositor.
Warehouse Keeper: The warehouse-keeper is responsible for issuing a signed warrant to any person lodging goods in their facility.
Warehouse Warrant: A warehouse warrant serves as a transferable document when endorsed, allowing the holder to receive the specified goods under the same conditions as the original depositor.
The form of the warehouse warrant must comply with requirements prescribed by the National Board of Revenue.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to prescribe the required form for warehouse warrants.
The Board is empowered to exempt specific classes of goods from the warrant requirements of this section through an official Gazette notification.
Goods: The National Board of Revenue may exempt certain classes of goods from the requirements governing warehouse warrants.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Control over warehoused goods
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
91. Control over warehoused goods.- (1) All warehoused goods shall be subject to the control of the appropriate officer.
(2) The appropriate officer may cause any warehouse, except a special bonded warehouse, to be locked.
(3) No person shall, without the written permission of the appropriate officer,-
(a) enter into a warehouse or remove any goods therefrom;
(b) unlock the warehouse which is locked under sub-section (2).
(4) Notwithstanding sub-section (1) any other officer of customs Inspection Directorate, Intelligence and Investigation Directorate, authorised in this behalf by an officer not below the rank of an Assistant Commissioner of Customs, shall have access to any part of a warehouse and power to examine the goods, records, accounts and documents therein and ask any question as may be deemed necessary.

Warehoused Goods: All warehoused goods are subject to the direct control of the appropriate officer of customs.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer has the authority to exercise control over all warehoused goods and may lock any warehouse, excluding special bonded warehouses.
Written permission from the appropriate officer is mandatory for any person to enter a warehouse, remove goods, or unlock a warehouse that has been officially locked.
Warehouse: Warehouses, other than special bonded warehouses, may be locked by the appropriate officer to maintain customs control.
Special Bonded Warehouse: Special bonded warehouses are exempt from the power of the appropriate officer to lock the premises under this section.
Customs Intelligence and Investigation D: Officers from this directorate, when authorized by an officer of at least the rank of Assistant Commissioner of Customs, have the right to access any warehouse.
These authorized officers are empowered to examine goods, records, accounts, and documents within a warehouse and may conduct necessary inquiries.
Assistant Commissioner of Customs: This officer holds the minimum rank required to authorize other customs officers from investigation or inspection directorates to access warehouses and examine goods and records.
Directorate of Inspection: Authorized officers from this directorate possess the authority to enter warehouses, inspect goods and records, and ask questions deemed necessary for official purposes.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to cause packages lodged in warehouse to be opened and examined
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
92. Power to cause packages lodged in warehouse to be opened and examined.- (1) The appropriate officer may at any time by order in writing direct that any goods or packages lodged in any warehouse shall be opened, weighed or otherwise examined; and after any goods have been so opened, weighed or examined, may cause the same to be sealed or marked in such manner as he thinks fit.
(2) When any goods have been so sealed and marked after examination, they shall not be again opened without the permission of the appropriate officer; and, when any such goods have been opened with such permission, the packages shall, if he thinks fit, be again sealed or marked.

Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer is empowered to issue written orders for the opening, weighing, or examination of any goods or packages stored in a warehouse at any time.
The officer has the authority to seal or mark examined goods as they deem appropriate.
The officer must provide permission before any previously sealed and marked goods are reopened, and they may mandate that these packages be resealed or remarked after the authorized opening.
Warehouse: Any goods or packages lodged within a warehouse are subject to being opened, weighed, or examined by an appropriate officer upon written direction.
Bonded Warehouse Goods: Once goods in a warehouse have been examined and sealed, they may not be opened again without official permission from the appropriate officer.
When such goods are opened with permission, the packages may be required to be resealed or marked again at the discretion of the appropriate officer.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Access of owners to warehoused goods
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
93. Access of owners to warehoused goods.- (1) Any owner of goods lodged in a warehouse shall, at any time within the hours of business, have access to his goods in the presence of an officer of customs, and an officer of customs shall, upon application for the purpose being made in writing to the appropriate officer, be deputed to accompany such owner.
(2) When an officer of customs is specially employed to accompany such owner, a sum sufficient to meet the expense thereby incurred shall, subject to rules, be paid by such owner to the appropriate officer, and such sum shall, if the appropriate officer so directs, be paid in advance.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of goods stored in a warehouse is entitled to access their goods during business hours.
The owner must request access in writing and may be required to pay the expenses incurred for a customs officer to accompany them, potentially in advance.
Warehouse: This is the facility where goods are lodged and where the owner is granted the right to access their items under official supervision.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer receives the written application from the owner to access warehoused goods and is responsible for deputing a customs officer to accompany the owner.
This officer is empowered to direct the payment of expenses for the customs officer's attendance and may require such payment to be made in advance.
Customs Officer: An officer of customs must be present to accompany the owner of the goods whenever they access their warehoused items.
The officer's attendance for such purposes is subject to rules regarding the recovery of expenses incurred.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Owner's power to deal with warehouse goods

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of warehoused goods is permitted to perform specific maintenance and commercial activities on their goods, provided they obtain the sanction of the appropriate officer and pay the prescribed fees.

Authorized activities for the owner include separating damaged goods, sorting goods, changing containers to ensure preservation, displaying goods for sale, and taking samples as allowed by the customs authority.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer must provide sanction before the owner can perform activities related to warehousing, sorting, or sampling goods.
The officer has the authority to permit the destruction of refuse, damaged, or surplus goods at the owner's request and may remit the duty payable on such destroyed items.
Bonded Warehouse Goods: These goods may be subjected to separation, repacking, or other treatments necessary for preservation, sale, or export while under customs control.
The officer may allow for the destruction of remaining refuse or damaged goods after repacking and may authorize the remission of duties on such discarded portions.
Duty Payment: The owner is required to pay prescribed fees to the appropriate officer to obtain authorization for dealing with warehoused goods.
Duty may be remitted by the appropriate officer for goods that are destroyed because they are damaged, surplus, or not worth the cost of the duty.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Manufacture and other operations in relation to goods in a warehouse
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
95. Manufacture and other operations in relation to goods in a warehouse.- (1) Subject to rules, the owner of any warehoused goods may, 1[by giving fifteen days prior notice in writing to the 2[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board]], carry on any manufacturing process or other operations in the warehouse in relation to such goods.
(2) Where in the course of any such operation or process there is any waste or refuse the following provisions shall apply, namely:-
(a) If the whole or any part of the goods produced by such operation or process are exported, no duty shall be charged on the quantity of the warehoused goods wasted or turned into refuse in the course of the operation or processing carried on in relation to the goods exported:
Provided that such waste or refuse is either destroyed or duty is paid on such waste or refuse as if it had been imported into 1[Bangladesh] in that form.
2[(b) If the whole or any part of the goods produced by such operation or process are cleared from the warehouse for home- consumption, duty and other taxes shall be charged on the quantity of such goods cleared for home-consumption and also on the warehoused goods wasted or turned into refuse in the course of the operation or processing carried on the relation to such goods cleared for home-consumption in a manner to be prescribed by rules:
Provided that the value for assessment purposes under this clause shall, notwithstanding any other provisions of this Act, be determined by the 3[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board].]

Warehoused Goods: The owner of warehoused goods may perform manufacturing processes or other operations on them within a warehouse, subject to prescribed rules and following a fifteen-day prior written notice to the authorized customs authority.
Commissioner of Customs: This official acts as the primary authority to receive notices for manufacturing operations in warehouses and is empowered to determine the value of waste or refuse for assessment purposes when goods are cleared for home consumption.
Bonded Warehouse Operation: Manufacturing and other operations performed on goods within a warehouse are subject to rules, and any resulting waste or refuse must be either destroyed or subjected to duties if the produced goods are cleared for export or home consumption.
Export Goods: No duty is charged on waste or refuse generated during the manufacturing process if the resulting final goods are exported, provided the waste is destroyed or appropriate duty is paid upon the waste itself.
Imported or Exported Goods: When goods produced from warehouse operations are cleared for home consumption, duties and taxes are applicable to both the cleared goods and any waste or refuse generated during the process as determined by prescribed rules.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Payment of rent and warehouse dues
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
96. Payment of rent and warehouse dues.- (1) The owner of any warehoused goods shall pay to the warehouse-keeper rent and other charges at the rates fixed under any law for the time being in force or where no rates are so fixed, at such rates as may be fixed by the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs or by agreement between the owner of the warehouse and the owner of warehoused goods.
(2) A table of the rates of rent and other charges fixed under sub- section (1) shall be displayed in a conspicuous part of such warehouse.
(3) If any rent or other charges are not paid within ten days from the date when they become due, the warehouse-keeper may, after due notice to the owner of the warehoused goods and with the permission of the appropriate officer, cause to be sold (any transfer of the warehoused goods notwithstanding) such portion of the goods as may be sufficient to realise the unpaid rent and other charges.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner is legally obligated to pay rent and other warehouse charges to the warehouse keeper at rates determined by law, by official designation, or by mutual agreement.
The owner is subject to the sale of their goods by the warehouse keeper if rent and charges remain unpaid after the prescribed notice period and with appropriate customs permission.
Warehouse Keeper: The warehouse keeper is entitled to collect rent and charges from the owner of warehoused goods at rates established by law or designated authorities.
The warehouse keeper is required to display a table of fixed rent and charge rates in a prominent location within the warehouse.

The warehouse keeper is empowered to sell a sufficient portion of the stored goods to recover unpaid rent and charges, provided that notice is given and the permission of the appropriate officer is obtained.
Commissioner of Customs: This authority is empowered to fix the rates for rent and warehouse charges in instances where no other rates have been established by law.
Warehouse: The facility must display a visible table outlining the fixed rates of rent and other charges applicable to the storage of goods.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer must provide the necessary permission before a warehouse keeper can sell stored goods to recover unpaid rent and charges.
Warehoused Goods: These goods are subject to rental and operational charges while stored in a warehouse.
A portion of these goods may be sold by the warehouse keeper to settle outstanding financial dues if payment is not made within the specified time frame following formal notice.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Goods not to be taken out of warehouse except as provided by this Act
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 97. Goods not to be taken out of warehouse except as provided by this Act.- No warehoused goods shall be taken out of any warehouse, except on clearance for home-consumption or export or for removal to another warehouse, or as otherwise provided in this Act.

Warehoused Goods: Warehoused goods may not be removed from a warehouse unless specific legal requirements for clearance are met.
Lawful removal of goods from a warehouse is limited to cases of home-consumption, export, removal to another warehouse, or other conditions explicitly permitted under the Customs Act 1969.
Customs Act 1969: The Act serves as the governing framework for the movement and clearance of warehoused goods.
It defines the exclusive conditions under which goods stored in a warehouse may be legally removed.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Period for which goods may remain warehoused
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
98. Period for which goods may remain warehoused. - (1) Goods imported for and warehoused in any special bonded warehouse or in any hundred percent export oriented industry, may remain in such warehouse or industry for a period not exceeding twenty four months from the date of warehousing :
(2) The Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorized by the Board in this behalf may extend the period of warehousing metioned in sub-section (1) for further period of six months if the goods specified in sub-section (1) are not likely to deteriorate.
[(2A) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-section (1) and (2), goods imported and warehoused by a hundred percent export oriented ship building industry, may remain in such warehouse for a period not exceeding forty eight months from the date of warehousing.]
(3) Goods imported for and warehoused in any diplomatic bonded warehouse, may remain in the warehouse for a period not exceeding twelve months from the date of warehousing.
(4) Warehoused goods other than the goods mentioned in sub-sections (1) and (3) may remain in the warehouse for a period not exceeding six months following the date of execution of the bond under section 86 in respect of such goods.
(5) In the case of any goods specified in sub-sections (3) and (4) which are not likely to deteriorate, the period for warehousing of such goods may, with reasons in writing, be extended by the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorized by the Board in this behalf for a period not exceeding three months and subsequently by the Board for a further period not exceeding three months.
(6) The Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorized by the Board in this behalf may reduce the period for warehousing mentioned in sub-sections (1), (3), and (4) to such reasonable period as he deems fit in each case, if the goods mentioned in such sub- sections are likely to deteriorate.]

Special Bonded Warehouse: Goods imported for and warehoused in a special bonded warehouse may remain stored for up to a specified maximum duration from the date of warehousing.
Export-Oriented Shipbuilding Industry: Goods imported and warehoused by a hundred percent export-oriented shipbuilding industry are permitted to remain in the warehouse for a specific extended period from the date of warehousing.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs (Bond) is empowered to extend warehousing periods for goods that are not expected to deteriorate, subject to specific conditions.
The Commissioner of Customs (Bond) has the authority to reduce the permitted warehousing period for goods that are likely to deteriorate to a reasonable duration.
National Board of Revenue: The Board may authorize Commissioners of Customs to manage and extend warehousing periods, and it retains the power to provide further extensions for goods that are not likely to deteriorate.
Warehoused Goods: The duration for which goods may be warehoused varies based on the type of warehouse and the nature of the goods, with specific limits established for different categories.

For various types of goods, authority is provided to extend or reduce the warehousing period depending on the likelihood of the goods deteriorating and the authorization from the competent customs authority.
Diplomatic Bonded Warehouse: Goods imported for and stored in a diplomatic bonded warehouse are subject to a maximum warehousing period from the date of warehousing.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Goods to be removed if licence is cancelled
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 98A. Goods to be removed if licence is cancelled.- When the licence of any private warehouse is cancelled, the owner of any goods warehoused therein shall, within ten days of the date on which notice of such cancellation is given or within such extended period as the appropriate officer may allow, remove the goods from that warehouse to another warehouse or clear them for home-consumption or exportation.]

Private Warehouse: The licence of a private warehouse may be cancelled, which triggers a mandatory removal of all warehoused goods by their owners.
Warehoused Goods: Following the cancellation of a private warehouse licence, owners of goods stored therein must relocate or clear their goods within ten days of receiving notice, or within an extended timeframe granted by the appropriate customs officer.
The owner of the goods has the options to move the items to another warehouse, clear them for home-consumption, or export them to ensure compliance with the cancellation of the warehouse licence.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer has the discretionary power to extend the period for removing goods from a private warehouse after its licence has been cancelled.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to remove goods from one warehouse to another in the same customs-station
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
99. Power to remove goods from one warehouse to another in the same customs-station.- (1) Any owner of goods warehoused under this Act may, within the period of their warehousing under section 98, and with the permission of the 2[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] 3[or any officer authorised for the purpose by the 2[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board],] on such conditions and after giving such security, if any, as 4[that commissioner] directs, remove goods from one warehouse to another warehouse in the same warehousing station.
(2) When any owner desires to remove any goods, he shall apply for permission to do so in such form as the Board may prescribe.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of warehoused goods is permitted to transfer their goods from one warehouse to another within the same warehousing station, provided this is done within the authorized warehousing period.
The owner must obtain official permission and provide any security as directed by the authorized customs official, and must submit a formal application in the format prescribed by the Board.
Commissioner of Customs: This authority, or any other Commissioner of Customs authorized by the Board, holds the power to grant permission for the removal of warehoused goods between warehouses at the same station.
This official has the power to set specific conditions for the transfer of goods and mandate the provision of security as a prerequisite for the removal.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the authority to authorize Commissioners of Customs to oversee the transfer of warehoused goods and is responsible for prescribing the application form required for such removal processes.
Warehousing Station: This represents the geographical or administrative jurisdiction where the transfer of warehoused goods between different warehouse facilities is permitted under the Act.
Bonded Warehouse: These facilities serve as the origin and destination points for the transfer of goods, governed by specific conditions and security requirements imposed by customs authorities.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to remove goods from one warehousing station to another
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
100. Power to remove goods from one warehousing station to another.- (1) Any owner of goods warehoused at any warehousing station may, within the period of their warehousing under section 98, remove the same for the purpose of warehousing them at any other warehousing station.
(2) When any owner desires to remove any goods for such purpose, he shall apply to the 5[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] in such form and manner as the Board may prescribe stating therein the particulars of the goods to be removed, and the name of the customs-station to which they are to be removed.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: An owner of warehoused goods is authorized to move their goods from one warehousing station to another within the period of warehousing permitted under the Act.

To initiate a transfer, the owner must apply to the appropriate customs authority by following the prescribed form and providing the required details about the goods and the destination customs station.
Warehousing Station: A warehousing station acts as a site where goods are stored under bond, and the law provides a legal mechanism for moving goods from one such station to another.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs (Bond), or another authorized Commissioner of Customs, is the designated authority responsible for reviewing and processing applications submitted by owners for the transfer of goods between warehousing stations.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to prescribe the specific forms, procedures, and conditions that owners must follow when applying to transfer warehoused goods between different stations.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Transmission of account of goods to officers at warehousing station of destination
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
101. Transmission of account of goods to officers at warehousing station of destination.- (1) When permission is granted for the removal of any goods from one warehousing station to another under section 100, an account containing the particulars thereof shall be transmitted by the appropriate officer of the customs-station of removal to the appropriate officer of the customs- station of destination.
(2) The person requiring the removal shall before such removal enter into a bond with one sufficient surety, in a sum equal at least to the duty chargeable on such goods, for the due arrival and re-warehousing thereof at the custom- station of destination, within such time, as the 1[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] directs.
(3) Such bond may be taken by the appropriate officer either at the customs-station of removal or at the customs-station of destination as best suits the convenience of the owner.
(4) If such bond is taken at customs-station of destination, a certificate thereof signed by the appropriate officer of such station shall at the time of the removal of such goods be produced to the appropriate officer at the customs- station of removal; and such bond shall not be discharged unless such goods are produced to the appropriate officer, and duly re-warehoused at the customs- station of destination within the time allowed for such removal or are otherwise accounted for to the satisfaction of such officer; nor until the full duty due upon any deficiency of such goods, not so accounted for, has been paid.
2[(5) Notwithstanding anything contained in the aforesaid sub-sections, the 3[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] may prescribe such conditions as he deems fit for the removal of warehoused goods from special bonded warehouse.]

Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is responsible for transmitting the particulars of warehoused goods when they are authorized for removal from one warehousing station to another.
They are authorized to accept the required bond for the removal of goods either at the station of removal or at the station of destination.
They ensure that warehoused goods are properly accounted for or re-warehoused at the destination within the allowed time, and they oversee the payment of duties on any deficiencies.
Warehousing Station: These stations serve as the origin and destination points for the movement of warehoused goods under customs control.
Warehoused Goods: The removal of these goods between warehousing stations requires specific documentation and the execution of a bond to ensure they arrive and are re-warehoused at the destination.
Commissioner of Customs: This authority determines the time limits within which goods removed from one warehousing station must arrive and be re-warehoused at the destination.
This authority may prescribe conditions for the removal of goods from a special bonded warehouse.
Special Bonded Warehouse: The removal of warehoused goods from this type of facility is subject to such conditions as the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) deems fit.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Remover may enter into a general bond
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 102. Remover may enter into a general bond.- The 4[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] may permit any person desirous of removing warehoused goods to enter into a general bond, with such sureties, in such amount and under such conditions as 5[that Commissioner] approves, for the removal, from time to time, of any goods from one warehouse to another, either in the same or in a different warehousing station and for the due arrival and re-warehousing of such goods at the destination within such time as 5[that Commissioner] directs.

Commissioner of Customs: This officer is empowered to authorize persons to enter into a general bond for the removal of warehoused goods.
An authorized Commissioner of Customs may approve the sureties, amounts, and conditions of a general bond used for moving goods between warehouses.
National Board of Revenue: The Board provides the authority for a Commissioner of Customs to permit the execution of general bonds.
Warehoused Goods: These goods may be removed from one warehouse to another under a general bond arrangement, subject to the requirement that they arrive and are re-warehoused at the destination within the time directed by the Commissioner.
Warehouse: Goods covered by a general bond may be moved between warehouses located within the same or different warehousing stations.
Warehousing Station: These stations serve as the origin and destination points for the transfer of bonded goods under a general bond.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Goods on arrival at customs-station of destination to be subject to same laws as goods on first importation
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 103. Goods on arrival at customs-station of destination to be subject to same laws as goods on first importation.- Upon the arrival of warehoused goods at the customs-station of destination, they shall be entered and warehoused in like manner as goods are entered and warehoused on the first importation thereof, and under the laws and rules, in so far as such laws and rules are applicable, which regulate the entry and warehousing of such last mentioned goods.

Warehoused Goods: Upon arrival at a customs station of destination, warehoused goods are subject to the same legal requirements and procedural rules for entry and warehousing as goods undergoing their first importation.
Customs Station: This is the designated location where warehoused goods must be entered and processed upon their arrival for the continuation of their warehousing status.
Importation: The processes governing the initial entry and storage of goods during their first importation serve as the legal benchmark for managing goods that have arrived at a customs station of destination.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Clearance of bonded goods for home-consumption
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
104. Clearance of bonded goods for home-consumption.- Any owner of warehoused goods may, at any time within the period of their warehousing under section 98, clear such goods for home-consumption by paying-
(a) the duty assessed on such goods under the provisions of this Act; and
(b) all rent, penalties, interest and other charges payable in respect of such goods6[:
Provided that necessary permission will have to be taken from 1[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] fifteen days in advance in case of Special Bonded Warehouse for special purposes to be determined by the 1[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board].]

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of warehoused goods is permitted to clear their goods for home-consumption at any time during the authorized warehousing period established under the Act.
Warehoused Goods: To clear warehoused goods for home-consumption, the owner must pay the assessed duties as well as all applicable rent, penalties, interest, and other associated charges.
Special Bonded Warehouse: For goods stored in a special bonded warehouse, the owner must obtain permission from the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or an authorized Commissioner of Customs at least fifteen days prior to clearing the goods for home-consumption.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or an authorized Commissioner of Customs has the authority to determine special purposes for which clearance must be pre-approved.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the authority to authorize specific Commissioners of Customs to manage permissions and determinations for special bonded warehouse activities.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Clearance of warehoused goods for export
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
105. Clearance of warehoused goods for export.- Any owner of warehoused goods may, at any time within the period of their warehousing under section 98, clear such goods for export out of 2[Bangladesh] on payment of all rent, penalties, interest and other charges payable as aforesaid but without paying any import duty thereon:
Provide that, if the 3[Government] is of the opinion that warehoused goods of any specified description are likely to be smuggled back into 2[Bangladesh], it may, by notification in the official Gazette, direct that such goods shall not be exported to any place outside 2[Bangladesh] without payment of duty or allow them to be exported subject to such restrictions and conditions as may be specified in the notification.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of warehoused goods is permitted to clear their goods for export at any time during the authorized warehousing period.
Export clearance is conditional upon the full payment of all relevant rent, interest, penalties, and associated charges.
Warehoused Goods: These goods may be cleared for export without the payment of import duty.
The government reserves the right to restrict the export of specific goods if there is a risk that they may be smuggled back into the country.
The government may mandate the payment of duty or impose specific conditions and restrictions on the export of certain warehoused goods via an official notification.
Government: The government has the authority to issue notifications in the official Gazette to restrict the export of certain goods if it determines that such goods are prone to being smuggled back into the country.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Clearance of warehoused goods for export as provisions, on a conveyance proceeding to foreign destination
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 106. Clearance of warehoused goods for export as provisions, on a conveyance proceeding to foreign destination.- Any warehoused provisions and stores may be exported within the period of their warehousing under section 98 without payment of import duty for use on board any conveyance proceeding to a foreign territory.

Warehoused Goods: Warehoused provisions and stores may be exported directly from a warehouse without payment of import duty, provided they are intended for use on board a conveyance departing for a foreign destination. This export process must be completed within the time limits prescribed for warehousing under the Act.
Conveyance: A conveyance intended for a foreign destination may take on warehoused stores and provisions as duty-free goods for use during its journey.
Import Duty: Import duty is waived for warehoused goods that are exported for use as provisions or stores on vessels or vehicles bound for a foreign territory.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Application for clearance of goods
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
107. Application for clearance of goods.- (1) An application to clear goods from any warehouse for home-consumption or for export shall be made in such form as the Board may prescribe.
(2) Such application shall ordinarily be made to the appropriate officer at least twenty-four hours before it is intended to clear such goods4[:
Provided that in the case of Special Bonded Warehouses, the procedure to be followed will be determined by 5[that 6[Commissioner] of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board.]

Application Form: The application to clear goods from a warehouse for home consumption or export must be submitted using a form prescribed by the National Board of Revenue.
Customs Clearance: Applications for the clearance of goods from a warehouse must be submitted to the appropriate officer at least twenty-four hours before the intended time of clearance.
Special Bonded Warehouse: For special bonded warehouses, the procedures for clearing goods are determined by the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or another customs commissioner authorized by the National Board of Revenue.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue holds the authority to prescribe the form for clearance applications and to authorize commissioners to determine specific procedures for special bonded warehouses.
Commissioner of Customs: This officer is responsible for determining the procedures to be followed for the clearance of goods from special bonded warehouses.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Re-assessment of warehoused goods when damaged or deteriorated
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 108. Re-assessment of warehoused goods when damaged or deteriorated.- If any goods upon which duties are levied ad valorem are damaged or deteriorated due to an unavoidable accident or cause after they have been entered for warehousing and assessed under section 80 and before they are cleared for home-consumption, their value in the damaged or deteriorated state may be appraised, if the owner so desires, by an officer of customs and the duty leviable thereon shall be diminished in proportion to the diminution of their value and a new bond for twice the amount of the diminished duty may, at the option of the owner, be executed by him to replace the bond originally executed. 1[** ** ** ** ** ** ** ** ** ** ** **]

Warehoused Goods: If goods are damaged or deteriorated due to unavoidable circumstances after being entered for warehousing but before clearance for home-consumption, the owner may request a re-assessment of their value.
The duty payable on such goods may be reduced in proportion to the decrease in their value resulting from the damage.
Officer of Customs: An officer of customs is authorized to appraise the value of damaged or deteriorated warehoused goods at the request of the owner to determine the adjusted duty.
Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner has the option to request a re-appraisal of damaged or deteriorated goods to seek a reduction in duty.
Upon re-assessment, the owner may choose to execute a new bond for twice the amount of the diminished duty to replace the bond originally provided.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Allowance in case of volatile goods
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 110. Allowance in case of volatile goods.- When any warehoused goods of such class or description as the Board having regard to the volatility of such goods and the manner of their storage may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify are, at the time of delivery from a warehouse, found to be deficient in quantity and the 2[Commissioner] of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] is satisfied that such deficiency is on account of natural loss, no duty shall be charged on such deficiency.

Warehoused Goods: The law allows for a deficiency in the quantity of certain volatile warehoused goods at the time of delivery from the warehouse.
No customs duty is chargeable on such deficiency if the relevant customs authority is satisfied that the loss was caused by natural factors during storage.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to specify by notification in the official Gazette which classes of goods qualify as volatile for the purpose of granting duty allowances on natural storage losses.
The Board also has the authority to authorize specific Commissioners of Customs to verify and approve such natural loss claims.
Commissioner of Customs: This official is authorized to review and satisfy themselves that a deficiency in warehoused goods is attributable to natural loss, thereby exempting the goods from customs duty on that missing portion.
Any Commissioner of Customs authorized by the Board may determine if a deficiency in volatile warehoused goods is due to natural causes, allowing for an exemption from duty on the lost quantity.
Warehouse: The provision applies to goods stored in a warehouse, specifically regarding the condition of the goods at the time they are delivered from the facility.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Duty on goods improperly removed from warehouse or allowed to remain beyond fixed time or lost or destroyed or taken as sample
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
111. Duty on goods improperly removed from warehouse or allowed to remain beyond fixed time or lost or destroyed or taken as sample.- In respect of goods specified hereunder the appropriate officer may demand and upon such demand the owner of such goods shall forthwith pay the full amount of duty chargeable on such goods together with all rent, penalties, interest and other charges payable in respect of them, namely :-
(a) Warehoused goods which are removed in contravention of section 97.
(b) Goods which have not been removed from the warehouse within the time allowed for such removal under section 98.
(c) Goods in respect of which a bond has been executed 3[under section 86 or as prescribed by rules made under this Act ]and which have not been cleared for home-consumption or export or removed in accordance with the provisions of this Act and are lost or destroyed otherwise than as provided in sections 94 and 95 or as mentioned in section 115, or are not accounted for to the satisfaction of the appropriate officer.
(d) Goods which have been taken under section 94 as samples without payment of duty.

Warehoused Goods: If these goods are removed from a warehouse in violation of the legal requirements, the owner must immediately pay the full amount of applicable duty, along with any accrued rent, penalties, interest, and other charges upon demand by the appropriate officer.

The owner is similarly liable for the full payment of duties and charges if the goods are not removed within the prescribed time limits or if they are lost, destroyed, or otherwise unaccounted for in a manner not authorized by law.
If goods are taken as samples without the payment of duty as permitted under the law, the owner remains liable for the full duty and associated charges upon demand.
Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner is legally obligated to pay the full amount of duty, rent, penalties, interest, and other charges upon demand by the appropriate officer when goods are improperly removed, left beyond the time limit, or lost or destroyed without proper authorization.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer has the authority to demand the payment of full duties and all associated charges from the owner when warehoused goods are removed, lost, destroyed, or treated in contravention of the Act.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Procedure on failure to pay duty, etc.
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
112. Procedure on failure to pay duty, etc.- 4[(1) If any owner fails to pay any sum demanded under section 111, the appropriate officer may either proceed upon the bond executed under 86 or as prescribed by rules made under this Act or cause such portion of the owners goods in the warehouse or any plant or machinery or equipment used for the manufacture of goods or any other goods and properties belonging to such persons to be detained as he may consider adequate to recover the demand, and the notice in writing for such detention, shall immediately be given to the owner.]
(2) In case the demand is not discharged within fifteen days of the date of such notice, the goods so detained may be sold.
(3) The net proceeds of any such sale shall be entered upon and adjusted against the bond and the surplus if any remaining after full satisfaction of the bond shall be disposed of in the manner provided in section 201.
(4) No transfer or assignment of the goods shall prevent the appropriate officer from proceeding against such goods in the manner above provided, for any amount due thereon.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: If the owner fails to pay any sum demanded by the customs authority regarding bonded goods, they are subject to enforcement actions such as bond recovery, detention of warehouse goods, or seizure of manufacturing assets.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer has the authority to recover outstanding duties by enforcing bonds, detaining the owner's goods or equipment, and ultimately selling detained assets if the demand remains unpaid after the specified period.
The officer's right to pursue recovery against goods is not affected by any subsequent transfer or assignment of those goods by the owner.
Warehouse: Goods stored within the warehouse are subject to detention and potential sale by the customs officer if the owner fails to discharge financial demands.
Detained Goods: If a financial demand issued to the owner remains unpaid for the prescribed period following a notice of detention, the goods may be sold to recover the amount due.
The proceeds from the sale of detained goods are used to satisfy the bond obligation, and any surplus funds are managed according to the provisions of the Customs Act.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal framework for the recovery of unpaid duties, including procedures for bond enforcement and the sale of detained property.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Noting removal of goods
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
113. Noting removal of goods.- (1) When any warehoused goods are taken out of any warehouse, the appropriate officer shall cause the fact to be noted on the back of the bond.
( 2) Every note so made shall specify the quantity and description of such goods, the purposes for which they have been removed, the date of removal, the name of the person removing them, the number and date of the bill of export under which they have taken away, if removed for exportation, or of the bill of entry, if removed for home-consumption and the amount of duty paid, if any.
1[(3) In case of Special Bonded warehouses, the procedure to be followed will be determined by the 2[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board.]

Warehoused Goods: The appropriate officer must record the removal of these goods on the back of the bond when they are taken out of a warehouse.

The record must include specific details regarding the goods, such as their quantity, description, the purpose of removal, the date of removal, the identity of the person removing them, the relevant export or entry documentation, and any applicable duties paid.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is responsible for documenting the removal of warehoused goods by noting the transaction on the back of the bond.
Bill of Export: This document is used when warehoused goods are removed for the purpose of exportation and must be referenced in the removal record.
Bill of Entry: This document is used when warehoused goods are removed for home consumption and must be referenced in the removal record.
Special Bonded Warehouse: The procedures for handling the removal of goods from these facilities are determined by the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or another authorized Commissioner.
Commissioner of Customs: This officer is authorized to determine the specific procedures for the removal of goods from special bonded warehouses.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to authorize a Commissioner of Customs to establish the procedures governing the removal of goods from special bonded warehouses.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Register of bonds
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
114. Register of bonds.- (1) A register shall be kept of all bonds entered into for customs-duties on warehoused goods, and entry shall be made in such register of all particulars required by section 113 to be specified 3[ , or in the case of Special Bonded warehouse entry shall be made in a register to be prescribed by the 4[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board].]
(2) When such register shows that the whole of the goods covered by any bond have been cleared for home-consumption or export, or otherwise duly accounted for, and when all amounts due on account of such goods have been paid, the appropriate officer shall cancel such bond as discharged in full, and shall on demand deliver the cancelled bond to the person who executed it or who is entitled to receive it.

Warehoused Goods: A register must be maintained to record all bonds executed for the payment of customs duties concerning warehoused goods.
Special Bonded Warehouse: For special bonded warehouses, entries must be made in a register specifically prescribed by the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or another Commissioner authorized by the Board.
Commissioner of Customs: This official is empowered to prescribe the register format used for recording entries related to special bonded warehouses.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: Once a bond is fully accounted for through home consumption, export, or other legal clearance, and all associated dues are paid, this officer is responsible for canceling the bond as discharged.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the authority to designate which Commissioners of Customs may authorize registers for special bonded warehouses.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to remit duties on warehoused goods lost or destroyed
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
115. Power to remit duties on warehoused goods lost or destroyed.- If any warehoused goods, in respect of which a bond has been executed under section 86 and which have not been cleared for home-consumption are lost or destroyed by unavoidable accident or cause, the 5[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] may in his discretion remit the duties due thereon:
Provided that, if any such goods be so lost or destroyed in a private warehouse, 6[notice thereof in writing shall] be given to the appropriate officer 6[within two working days] after the discovery of such loss or destruction.

Warehoused Goods: If these goods are lost or destroyed due to an unavoidable accident or cause before they are cleared for home-consumption, the duties payable on them may be remitted.
The remission of duties on these goods is subject to the discretion of the Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or another authorized Commissioner.
Commissioner of Customs: This official has the discretionary power to remit the customs duties on warehoused goods that have been lost or destroyed due to unavoidable circumstances before home-consumption clearance.
Private Warehouse: If warehoused goods are lost or destroyed while held in a private warehouse, the owner is required to provide written notice to the appropriate officer within a set period after the event is discovered.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer must be notified in writing of any loss or destruction of goods occurring within a private warehouse within two working days of the discovery of the incident.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Responsibility of warehouse-keeper
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
116. Responsibility of warehouse-keeper.- The warehouse-keeper in respect of goods lodged in a public warehouse, and the licensee in respect of goods lodged in a private warehouse, shall be responsible for their due receipt therein and delivery therefrom, and their safe custody while deposited therein, according to the quantity, weight or gauge reported by the officer of customs who has assessed such goods, allowance being made, if necessary, for deficiency in quantity on account of natural loss as provided in section 110:
Provided that no owner of goods shall be entitled to claim from the appropriate officer or from any keeper of a public warehouse, compensation for any loss or damage occurring to such goods while they are being passed into or out of such warehouse, or while they remain therein, unless it be proved that such loss or damage was occasioned by the wilful act or neglect of the warehouse-keeper or of an officer of customs.
1[117 ** ** **] 
2[117A ** ** **]

Warehouse Keeper: The warehouse keeper is legally responsible for the proper receipt, safe custody, and delivery of goods lodged in a public warehouse according to the quantities recorded upon assessment.
They may be held liable for loss or damage to goods if it is proven that such harm resulted from their wilful act or neglect.
Licensee: The licensee is legally responsible for the proper receipt, safe custody, and delivery of goods lodged in a private warehouse according to the quantities recorded upon assessment.
Public Warehouse: Goods lodged in a public warehouse are subject to the responsibility of the warehouse keeper for their receipt, storage, and delivery.
Private Warehouse: Goods lodged in a private warehouse are subject to the responsibility of the licensee for their receipt, storage, and delivery.
Officer of Customs: The officer of customs is responsible for initially assessing the quantity, weight, or gauge of goods entering the warehouse.
The officer of customs is not liable for loss or damage to goods in the warehouse unless such damage resulted from their wilful act or neglect.
Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of warehoused goods is not entitled to compensation from the customs authority or warehouse keepers for loss or damage to goods unless such damage was caused by wilful act or neglect.
Customs Act 1969: The Act provides the legal basis for holding warehouse keepers and licensees accountable for the safe custody of deposited goods, while acknowledging permissible natural losses as defined in section 110.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to decide where goods may be deposited in warehouse, and on what terms
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 118. Power to decide where goods may be deposited in 3[warehouse], and on what terms.- The 4[Commissioner of Customs (Bond) or any other Commissioner of Customs authorised by the Board] may from time to time determine in what division of any 5[warehouse], and in what manner, and on what terms, any goods may be deposited, and what sort of goods may be deposited in any such warehouse.

Warehouse: The appropriate customs authority has the power to determine the specific divisions of a warehouse where goods may be stored.
The authority may regulate the manner and terms under which goods are deposited, as well as define the specific types of goods permitted for storage in a given warehouse.
Commissioner of Customs: This officer is empowered to decide the operational terms, storage divisions, and the categories of goods allowed within a warehouse.
Any Commissioner of Customs authorized by the Board may exercise the power to regulate the deposit of goods in warehouses.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the authority to empower specific Commissioners of Customs to manage and determine terms for the storage of goods in warehouses.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Expenses of carriage, packing, etc., to be borne by owner
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 119. Expenses of carriage, packing, etc., to be borne by owner.- The expenses of carriage, packing and storage of goods on their receipt into or removal from a public warehouse shall, if paid by the appropriate officer or by the warehouse-keeper, be chargeable on the goods and be defrayed by, and recoverable from, the owner, in the manner provided in section 112.

Goods: The costs related to the carriage, packing, and storage of goods when they are received into or removed from a public warehouse are deemed a charge upon the goods themselves.
These expenses must be paid by the owner of the goods and are recoverable in the same manner as prescribed for the recovery of warehouse rent.
Public Warehouse: The operational expenses for receiving or removing goods at a public warehouse are subject to specific cost recovery rules.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: If the appropriate officer incurs expenses for the carriage, packing, or storage of goods, they are entitled to recover these costs from the owner of the goods.
Warehouse Keeper: If the warehouse keeper incurs expenses for the carriage, packing, or storage of goods, they are entitled to recover these costs from the owner of the goods.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to add, alter or relax the condition, etc.
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 119A. Power to add, alter or relax the condition, etc.- The 7[Board] may, by notification in the official Gazette, add or alter any condition or requirement contained in any provision of this chapter, and if it considers expedient, relax any provision thereof, to meet any special requirement.]

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is empowered to issue notifications in the official Gazette to modify, add to, or relax conditions and requirements within this chapter of the Customs Act 1969. This authority is granted to provide the Board with flexibility in addressing special requirements as they arise.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the foundational authority for the National Board of Revenue to adjust regulatory conditions and relax its provisions through official gazette notifications when deemed expedient.

processed_clauses.metadata_title: CHAPTER XII TRANSHIPMENT
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
CHAPTER XII
TRANSHIPMENT

Transshipment: This chapter of the Customs Act 1969 establishes the legal framework and regulatory provisions governing the transshipment of goods within the customs jurisdiction.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Chapter not to apply to baggage or postal articles
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 120. Chapter not to apply to baggage or postal articles.- The provisions of this Chapter shall not apply to (a) baggage, and (b) goods imported by post.

Baggage: The provisions of this chapter of the Customs Act do not apply to baggage.
Postal Articles: The provisions of this chapter of the Customs Act do not apply to goods imported by post.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Transhipment of goods without payment of duty
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 121. Transhipment of goods without payment of duty.- Subject to the provisions of section 15 and the rules, the appropriate officer may, on application by the owner of any goods imported at any customs-station and specially and distinctly manifested at the time of importation as for transhipment to some other customs-station or foreign destination, grant leave to tranship the same without payment of duty, if any, chargeable on such goods at the customs-station of transhipment and, in case of goods to be transhipped to some other customs- station, with or without any security or bond for the due arrival and entry of the goods thereat.

Imported Goods: These goods may be transhipped without the payment of duty if they were specially and distinctly manifested for transhipment at the time of their original importation.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer has the authority to grant leave for the transhipment of goods after receiving an application from the owner of the imported goods.
Customs Station: This is the location where the goods arrive and are processed for transhipment to another customs-station or a foreign destination.
Security Bond: The appropriate officer may require a security or bond to ensure the due arrival and proper entry of goods that are being transhipped to another customs-station.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Superintendence of transhipment
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 122. Superintendence of transhipment.- An officer of customs shall in every case, be deputed free of charge to superintend the removal of transhipped goods from one conveyance to another.

Officer of Customs: An officer of customs is responsible for overseeing the process whenever goods are being transhipped from one conveyance to another.
The services of the customs officer for the purpose of this superintendence must be provided free of charge.
Conveyance: This entity refers to the vehicles or vessels involved in the movement of goods, where the transhipment process requires customs supervision during the transfer between them.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Entry, etc., of transhipped goods
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 123. Entry, etc., of transhipped goods.- All goods transhipped under section 121 to any customs-station shall, on their arrival at such customs-station, be entered in the same manner as goods on their first importation and shall be dealt with like-wise.

Goods in Transit: Goods that are transhipped to a customs station are subject to the same entry requirements and legal procedures as those applicable to goods upon their first importation into the country.
Customs Station: Upon the arrival of transhipped goods at a customs station, the facility must ensure that these goods are processed and handled according to the standard procedures governing the importation of goods.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Transhipment of provisions and stores from one conveyance to another of the same owner without payment of duty
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 124. Transhipment of provisions and stores from one conveyance to another of the same owner without payment of duty.- Any provisions and stores in use or being carried for use on board a conveyance may, at the discretion of the appropriate officer be transhipped to another conveyance belonging wholly or partly to the same owner and present simultaneously at the same customs-station, without payment of duty.

Stores and Provisions: Provisions and stores being used or carried on board a conveyance may be transhipped to another vessel under specific conditions without the requirement to pay duty.
Conveyance: A conveyance may receive stores and provisions via transhipment from another conveyance owned by the same person, provided both vessels are present at the same customs station at the same time.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer has the discretionary power to permit the duty-free transhipment of stores and provisions between conveyances belonging to the same owner.
Customs Station: Transhipment of stores and provisions without payment of duty is only permitted when both the original and receiving conveyances are present simultaneously at the same customs-station.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Levy of transhipment fees
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 125. Levy of transhipment fees.- Subject to the rules, a transhipment fee on any goods or class of goods transhipped under this Act may be levied at such rates, according to weight, measurement, quantity, number, bale, package or container, as the Board may, by notification in the official Gazette, prescribe for any customs-station or class of customs-stations.

Goods: Transhipment fees may be levied on any goods or classes of goods that are transhipped under the provisions of the Customs Act 1969.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to prescribe transhipment fee rates through notifications in the official Gazette. These rates may vary based on factors such as weight, measurement, quantity, or packaging type and can be specified for particular customs stations or classes of customs stations.
Customs Station: The Board is empowered to prescribe specific transhipment fee structures applicable to any individual customs station or a designated class of customs stations.
Rules: The levying of transhipment fees is subject to the conditions and regulations prescribed by the relevant rules.

processed_clauses.metadata_title: CHAPTER XIII TRANSIT TRADE
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
CHAPTER XIII
TRANSIT TRADE

Transit Trade: This chapter establishes the foundational legal framework and regulatory provisions governing transit trade within the jurisdiction of the Customs Act 1969.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Chapter not to apply to baggage or postal articles
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 126. Chapter not to apply to baggage or postal articles.- The provisions of this Chapter shall not apply to (a) baggage, and (b) goods imported by post.

Baggage: The provisions of this Chapter of the Customs Act 1969 do not apply to baggage.
Postal Articles: The provisions of this Chapter of the Customs Act 1969 do not apply to goods imported by post.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Transit of goods in the same conveyance
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
127. Transit of goods in the same conveyance.- (1) Subject to the provisions of section 15 and the rules any goods imported in a conveyance and mentioned in the import manifest as for transit in the same conveyance to a customs-station in 1[Bangladesh] or to any destination outside 1[Bangladesh] may be allowed to be so transited without payment of duty, if any, leviable on such goods at the customs-station of transit.
(2) Any stores and provisions imported on board a conveyance which is in transit through 1[Bangladesh] to a destination outside 1[Bangladesh], may subject to rules, be allowed to be consumed on board that conveyance without payment of the duties which would otherwise be chargeable on them.

Goods in Transit: Goods imported in a conveyance and declared in the import manifest for transit to a destination within or outside the country may be transited without payment of duties at the customs station of transit, subject to relevant rules and statutory provisions.
Stores and Provisions: Stores and provisions imported on a conveyance transiting through the country may be consumed on board without payment of duty, subject to compliance with the rules.
Conveyance: A conveyance is recognized as the vehicle for transporting goods in transit or carrying stores and provisions that may be consumed during the transit journey.
Import Manifest: The import manifest serves as the official document required to identify goods as intended for transit in the same conveyance.
Customs Station: The customs station serves as the designated location to which goods may be transited under the provisions of the Customs Act.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Transport of certain classes of goods subject to prescribed conditions
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 128. Transport of certain classes of goods subject to prescribed conditions.- Any goods may be transported from one part of 1[Bangladesh] to another through any foreign territory, subject to such conditions as to their due arrival at the destination as may be prescribed by rules.

Goods: Goods may be transported between different parts of Bangladesh by passing through foreign territory.
The transport of such goods is subject to specific conditions set by rules to ensure their arrival at the intended destination.
Rules: The government may issue rules that establish the mandatory conditions for the transit of goods through foreign territory to ensure they reach their destination within Bangladesh.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Transit of goods across Bangladesh to a foreign territory
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 129. Transit of goods across 1[Bangladesh] to a foreign territory.- Where any goods are entered for transit across 1[Bangladesh] to a destination outside 1[Bangladesh], the appropriate officer may, subject to the provisions of the rules, allow the goods to be so transited without payment of the duties which would otherwise be chargeable on such goods. 30[]

Transit Goods: Goods entered for transit across Bangladesh to a foreign destination may be permitted to pass through the territory under the authority of the appropriate customs officer.
The transit of these goods is permitted without the payment of import or export duties that would normally be applicable under the Customs Act.
