Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer has the discretionary power to allow the transit of goods across Bangladesh subject to the provisions of the established rules.
Rules: The transit of goods across the country is subject to compliance with the relevant rules established under the Customs Act.

processed_clauses.metadata_title: CHAPTER XIV EXPORTATION OR SHIPMENT AND RELANDING
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
CHAPTER XIV
EXPORTATION OR SHIPMENT AND RELANDING

Export: This chapter governs the legal procedures and regulatory frameworks applicable to the exportation or shipment of goods, as well as the conditions concerning the relanding of goods that were intended for export.

processed_clauses.clause_title: No goods to be loaded on a conveyance, till entry outwards or permission granted
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 130. No goods to be loaded on a conveyance, till entry outwards or permission granted.- No goods other than passengers baggage or mail bags or ballast urgently required for a vessels safety shall be loaded or water-borne to be loaded on a conveyance at a place in a customs-station approved for the purpose under clause (b) of section 10, until an order under section 50 in respect of the conveyance has been given or permission in this behalf in writing has been granted by the appropriate officer.

Goods: The loading of goods onto a conveyance at an approved customs station is strictly prohibited until the required entry outward or written permission is granted by the appropriate customs officer.
Exceptions to this loading restriction are provided for passenger baggage, mail bags, and ballast that is urgently required for the safety of a vessel.
Conveyance: A conveyance cannot be loaded with goods at an approved customs station unless formal entry outward has been obtained or explicit written permission has been granted by the appropriate officer.
Customs Station: The prohibition on loading goods applies to any place within a customs station that has been specifically approved for such operations under the relevant section of the Act.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer holds the authority to grant the necessary written permission required to load goods onto a conveyance prior to the formal entry outward order.
Passenger or Crew Baggage: This category of goods is exempted from the general restriction on loading a conveyance before entry outward is granted.
Mail Bags: Mail bags are permitted to be loaded onto a conveyance without waiting for the formal entry outward order or prior written permission.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Clearance for exportation
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
131. Clearance for exportation.- 2[1] No goods shall be loaded for exportation until-
(a) in the case of goods other than passengers' baggage and mail bag-
3[(i) the owner has delivered to the appropriate officer or, if the owner is a registered user, he has transmitted to the Customs computer system, a bill of export in such for in and manner and containing such particulars as the Board may, by order, direct from time to time 4[:
Provided that the Commissioner of Customs may within a period of six months require the owner who has electronically transmitted a bill of export to the Customs computer system to submit to the appropriate officer a paper bill of export duly signed by him or his authorized agent containing such information as the said Commissioner may specify;]
(ii) such owner has paid the duties payable on such goods;
(iii) such bill has been passed by the appropriate officer; and
(b) in the case of passengers' baggage or mail bags, the appropriate officer has permitted them to be exported :
Provided that the Board may in the case of any customs-station or wharf, by notification in the official Gazette, and subject to such restrictions and conditions, if any, as it thinks fit, exempt any specified goods or class of goods or any specified person or class of persons, from all or any of the provisions of this section5[:
Provided further that where the appropriate officer, in a particular case, has reason to believe that exportation of any goods in respect of which exemption has been notified under the first proviso should be intervened before its loading for exportation, he may, upon recording reasons, examine the goods or the bill of export or both, and may take other necessary action under this Act.]
1[(2) In a case where exemption has been allowed under the proviso to sub-section (1) and any goods have been exported subject of any conditions or under any guarantee or undertaking, the exporter shall forthwith fulfil such conditions or, as the case may be, the terms of the guarantee or undertaking and submit to the appropriate officer documents relating thereto, including proceeds realisation certificate or such other documentary evidence showing the remittance to Bangladesh of the sale proceeds of the goods exported as may be acceptable to the Board.]

Export: No goods shall be loaded for exportation unless specific procedural requirements are met, including the filing of a bill of export, payment of applicable duties, and clearance by the appropriate officer.
The Board has the authority to exempt specific goods or classes of persons from the standard exportation clearance procedures at customs stations or wharves.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is responsible for receiving the bill of export, passing the bill, and granting permission for the export of passengers' baggage or mail bags.

The officer may require the submission of a paper bill of export for goods previously transmitted electronically and has the authority to examine goods even when exemptions have been granted if there is reason to believe intervention is necessary.
Bill of Export: The owner must deliver or electronically transmit a bill of export containing specified particulars before goods can be loaded for exportation.
The Commissioner of Customs may request a signed paper copy of an electronically transmitted bill of export within a specified timeframe.
Registered User: A registered user may fulfill the documentation requirements for exportation by electronically transmitting the bill of export to the customs computer system.
Exporter: When goods are exported under an exemption, guarantee, or undertaking, the exporter is obligated to fulfill all associated conditions and submit documentary evidence, such as proof of export proceeds realization, to the appropriate officer.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the power to direct the format and particulars of the bill of export and can grant exemptions from exportation procedures through official gazette notifications.
Baggage: The exportation of passengers' baggage requires permission from the appropriate officer, subject to specific regulatory conditions.
Mail Bags: The exportation of mail bags requires permission from the appropriate officer before loading can proceed.
Customs Station: The Board may specify exemptions for goods or persons from exportation provisions at specific customs-stations or wharves via official notification.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Bond required in certain cases before exportation
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 132. Bond required in certain cases before exportation.- Before any warehoused goods subject to excise duties, or goods entitled to drawback or repayment of customs-duties on exportation, or goods exportable only under particular rules or restrictions, are permitted to be exported, the owner shall, if required so to do, give security by bond in such sum not exceeding twice the duty leviable on such goods as the appropriate officer directs, with one sufficient surety, that such goods shall be exported and landed at the place for which they are entered outwards or shall be otherwise accounted for to the satisfaction of such officer.

Warehoused Goods: These goods may be subject to excise duties, and their exportation requires specific bonding procedures if mandated by the customs authority.
Customs Duty Drawback: Goods eligible for a drawback or repayment of duties upon exportation may be subject to mandatory security bond requirements before export is permitted.
Export: The exportation of specific categories of goods, such as those under bond or restriction, is conditional upon the owner providing security for their safe transit and landing at the declared destination.
Security Bond: Owners of certain goods intended for export must provide a security bond, at the direction of the appropriate officer, in an amount up to twice the leviable duty to ensure the goods are exported and accounted for properly.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is empowered to require the owner of goods to provide a security bond before exportation and must be satisfied that the goods are accounted for at their destination.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Additional charge on goods cleared for export after port-clearance granted
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 133. Additional charge on goods cleared for export after port- clearance granted.- Where the goods are cleared for shipment on a bill of export presented after port-clearance or permission to depart has been granted, the appropriate officer may, if he thinks fit, levy, in addition to any duty to which such goods are ordinarily liable, a charge not exceeding one percent of the value of the goods determined in accordance with the provisions of section 25.

Export Goods: These goods may be subjected to an additional charge if they are cleared for shipment after the port-clearance or permission to depart has already been granted.
Bill of Export: This document is used for the clearance of export goods, and its presentation after the grant of port-clearance or departure permission may trigger an additional charge on the goods.
Port Clearance: The granting of port-clearance marks a key administrative milestone in the export process, beyond which the presentation of a bill of export may result in an additional charge.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer has the discretionary power to levy an additional charge, not exceeding a specified percentage of the value of the goods, when the export process is delayed beyond the granting of port-clearance.
Value: The value of the goods, as determined by the provisions of the Act, serves as the basis for calculating the maximum limit of the additional charge that may be imposed by the customs officer.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Notice of non-loading or relanding and return of duty thereon
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
134. Notice of non-loading or relanding and return of duty thereon.- (1) If any goods mentioned in a bill of export or manifest be not loaded or be loaded and afterwards relanded, the owner shall before the expiration of fifteen clear working days after the conveyance on which such goods were intended to be loaded or from which they were relanded has left the customs-station, give information of such short-loading or relanding to the appropriate officer save where the latter has occasioned the short-loading or relanding.
(2) Upon an application being made to the appropriate officer within one year of such short-loading or relanding any duty levied upon goods not loaded or upon goods loaded and afterwards relanded shall be refunded to the person on whose behalf such duty was paid:
Provided that, where the required information of short-loading or relanding is not given within the aforesaid period of fifteen days, the appropriate officer may make refund of duty contingent upon payment of such penalty, if any, as he may see fit to impose.

Goods: The owner is required to provide information regarding any goods that were intended for export but were not loaded onto the conveyance or were relanded after loading.
Duty paid on goods that were not loaded or were relanded is subject to refund, provided that the required notification was given and a formal application was submitted.
Bill of Export: This document is used to record goods intended for export, and discrepancies such as non-loading or relanding must be reported in accordance with procedures linked to it.
Manifest: This document serves as an official record of cargo, and the notification procedures for short-loading or relanding apply to goods listed herein.
Conveyance: The owner of the goods must report short-loading or relanding within a specified timeframe after the conveyance has departed from the customs-station.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is responsible for receiving notifications regarding non-loading or relanding of goods and processing applications for the refund of duties.
The officer has the discretion to impose a penalty for failures to report such occurrences within the specified fifteen-day period before authorizing a refund of duty.
Refund of Customs Duty: A refund of duty can be claimed within one year for goods that were not loaded or were relanded, provided proper notification was given.
The officer may make the granting of a refund contingent upon the payment of a penalty if the initial notification of non-loading or relanding was delayed.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Goods relanded or transhipped from a conveyance returning to a customs-station or putting into another customs-station
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
135. Goods relanded or transhipped from a conveyance returning to a customs-station or putting into another customs-station.- (1) If, after having cleared from any customs-station any conveyance without having discharged her cargo returns to such customs-station or puts into any other customs-station, any owner of goods in such conveyance, if he desires to land or tranship the same or any portion thereof for re-export, may, with the consent of the person-in-charge of the conveyance, apply to the appropriate officer in that behalf.
(2) The appropriate officer, if he grants the application, shall thereupon send an officer of customs to watch the conveyance and to take charge of such goods during such relanding or transhipment.
(3) Such goods shall not be allowed to be transhipped or re-exported free of duty by reason of the previous settlement of duty at the time of first export unless they are lodged and remain, until the time of re-export under the custody of an officer of customs, in a place appointed by the appropriate officer, or are transhipped under such custody.
(4) All expenses attending such custody shall be borne by the owner.

Customs Station: A conveyance that has cleared from a customs-station may return to it or put into another customs-station if it has not discharged its cargo.
The process of relanding or transhipping goods from such a conveyance at a customs-station is subject to regulatory oversight by the appropriate officer.
Conveyance: A conveyance that returns to a customs-station without having discharged its cargo may allow goods on board to be relanded or transhipped for re-export.
The owner of goods on board must obtain the consent of the person in charge of the conveyance to land or tranship such goods.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer of customs has the authority to grant or deny applications for the relanding or transhipment of goods from a returning conveyance.
If an application is granted, the officer must assign an officer of customs to supervise the handling of the goods and appoint a specific place for their custody.
Officer of Customs: An officer of customs is tasked with watching the conveyance and taking charge of goods during the relanding or transhipment process.
Goods intended for re-export must remain under the custody of an officer of customs in an appointed place to maintain eligibility for duty-related conditions.
Goods: Owners of goods on a returning conveyance may apply to reland or tranship them for re-export with the required consent and administrative approval.
Such goods are not automatically exempt from duty upon re-export based on initial duty settlement unless they are kept under official customs custody until the time of re-export.
All expenses related to the official custody of these goods during the relanding or transhipment process are the responsibility of the owner.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Conveyance returning to customs-station may enter and land goods
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
136. Conveyance returning to customs-station may enter and land goods.- (1) In either of the cases mentioned in section 135, the person-in-charge of the conveyance may enter such conveyance inwards and any owner of goods thereon may, with the consent of the person-in-charge of conveyance, land the same under the provisions of this Act and the rules.
(2) In every such case, any export duty paid shall be refunded on an application made by the owner of such goods within one year of their landing and any amount paid to owners as drawback or repayment of duty (whether of customs, excise or any other tax) shall be recovered from him or adjusted against the amount refundable.

Conveyance: If a conveyance is forced to return to a customs-station, the person in charge may enter the conveyance inwards after its return.
When a conveyance returns to a customs-station, the owner of the goods on board may land the goods provided they have the consent of the person in charge of the conveyance.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance that has returned to a customs-station has the authority to enter the conveyance inwards.
The person in charge of a conveyance controls whether or not the owners of goods on board are permitted to land their goods upon returning to a customs-station.
Export Duty: If goods are landed after a conveyance returns to a customs-station, any export duty previously paid on those goods is eligible for a refund.
Customs Duty Drawback: If a refund is claimed for goods landed after a conveyance returns, any previously issued drawback or tax repayment related to those goods must be recovered from the owner or adjusted against the refund amount.
Customs Station: This station serves as the location where a returning conveyance may enter inwards and where goods on board may be landed by their owners.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Landing of goods during repairs
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
137. Landing of goods during repairs.- (1) The appropriate officer may, on application by the person-in-charge of a conveyance which is obliged before completing her journey or voyage to put into any customs-station for repairs, permit him to land the goods or any portion thereof, and to place it in the custody of an officer of customs during such repairs, and to load and export the same free of duty.
(2) All expenses attending such custody shall be borne by the person-in- charge of the conveyance.

Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer has the discretionary authority to permit the offloading of goods from a conveyance that has arrived at a customs station for necessary repairs prior to completing its journey.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge may apply to the appropriate officer for permission to land goods when their conveyance requires repairs at a customs station.
The person in charge is responsible for bearing all expenses related to the custody of the goods during the period of repair.
Customs Custody: Goods landed for the purpose of conveyance repairs are required to be placed under the custody of an officer of customs.
Export of Goods: Goods that were landed for the purpose of repairs may be re-loaded and exported without the payment of customs duty.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Frustrated cargo and other than frustrated cargo how dealt with
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
138. Frustrated cargo 31[and other than frustrated cargo] how dealt with.- (1) Where any goods are brought into a customs-station by reason of inadvertence, mis-direction or untraceability of the consignee, the 1[Commissioner of Customs] may, on application by the person-in-charge of the conveyance which brought such goods or of the consignor of such goods and subject to rules, allow export of such goods without payment of any duties (whether of import or export) chargeable thereon, provided that such goods have remained and are exported under the custody of an officer of customs.
32[(1A) Where any goods are brought into a customs-station by a reason other than the reasons mentioned in sub-section (1), the Commissioner of Customs may, with prior approval of the Board, allow re-exportation of such goods without payment of any duties chargeable thereon.]
(2) All expenses attending to such custody shall be borne by the applicant.

Frustrated Cargo: Frustrated cargo refers to goods brought into a customs station due to inadvertence, misdirection, or the untraceability of the consignee. The Commissioner of Customs may permit the export of such goods without payment of import or export duties, provided the goods remain under customs custody until their departure.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is authorized to approve the export of frustrated cargo upon application by the person in charge of the conveyance or the consignor, subject to established rules and the condition of maintaining customs custody.

For goods brought into a customs station under circumstances other than those classified as frustrated cargo, the Commissioner of Customs may authorize re-exportation without duty payment, provided prior approval from the National Board of Revenue is obtained.
Customs Station: A customs station serves as the designated location for the management and handling of frustrated cargo and other goods eligible for re-exportation.
Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance that brought goods into a customs station may apply to the Commissioner of Customs for the export of frustrated cargo without payment of duties.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue must provide prior approval before the Commissioner of Customs can authorize the re-exportation of goods that do not meet the legal criteria for frustrated cargo.
Customs Custody: Goods designated for export as frustrated cargo must remain under the continuous custody of an officer of customs throughout the process to qualify for duty exemptions.
All expenses incurred while goods are held in customs custody must be paid by the applicant who requested the export or re-exportation.

processed_clauses.metadata_title: CHAPTER XV SPECIAL PROVISIONS REGARDING BAGGAGE AND GOODS IMPORTED OR EXPORTED BY POST
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
CHAPTER XV
SPECIAL PROVISIONS REGARDING BAGGAGE
AND GOODS IMPORTED OR EXPORTED BY POST

Baggage: This chapter establishes special legal provisions governing the handling, declaration, and clearance of baggage under the Customs Act 1969.
Postal Goods: This chapter provides the regulatory framework and special procedures for goods that are imported or exported through the postal system.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Declaration by passenger or crew of baggage
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 139. Declaration by passenger or crew of baggage.- The owner of any baggage whether a passenger or a member of the crew shall, for the purpose of clearing it, make a verbal or written declaration of its contents in such manner as may be prescribed by rules to the appropriate officer and shall answer such questions as the said officer may put to him with respect to his baggage and any article contained therein or carried with him and shall produce such baggage and any such article for examination.

Passenger or Crew: A passenger or crew member who owns baggage is required to declare the contents of that baggage, either verbally or in writing, to the customs authorities for the purpose of clearance.
A passenger or crew member must answer any questions asked by an officer regarding their baggage and any articles carried with them, and they must present such items for customs examination.
Baggage: Baggage owned by passengers or crew must be formally declared and produced for examination by the appropriate customs officer to facilitate the customs clearance process.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer has the authority to receive declarations from passengers or crew, question them regarding their belongings, and examine the baggage and articles presented.
Rules: The manner and form in which a passenger or crew member must provide a declaration for their baggage are determined by the rules prescribed under the Act.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Determination of rate of duty in respect of baggage
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 140. Determination of rate of duty in respect of baggage.- The rate of duty if any, applicable to baggage shall be the rate in force on the date on which a declaration is made in respect of such baggage under section 139.

Baggage: The rate of customs duty applicable to baggage is determined based on the legal rate in force at the time the declaration is made.
Customs Duty Rate: The applicable rate of duty for imported baggage is fixed by the duty rate in effect on the date a formal baggage declaration is submitted under the relevant section of the Customs Act 1969.
Baggage Declaration: The submission of a baggage declaration serves as the reference point for determining the effective date for applying customs duty rates to the goods being declared.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Bona fide baggage exempt from duty
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 141. Bona fide baggage exempt from duty.- The appropriate officer may, subject to the limitations, conditions and restriction specified in the rules, pass free of duty any article in the baggage of a passenger or a member of the crew in respect of which the said officer is satisfied that it is bona fide meant for the use of such passenger or for making gift.

Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer is empowered to allow the duty-free clearance of baggage items, provided they are satisfied that the items are intended for personal use or for gifting.
Bona Fide Baggage: Articles within the baggage of a passenger or crew member may be exempted from duty if they are deemed to be for the personal use of the passenger or as gifts.
The exemption of bona fide baggage is subject to the specific limitations, conditions, and restrictions established in the relevant rules.
Passenger or Crew: Baggage belonging to passengers or crew members qualifies for duty-free consideration under the conditions defined by the rules and the satisfaction of the customs officer.
Rules: The rules govern the limitations, conditions, and restrictions under which the appropriate officer may permit the duty-free import of bona fide baggage.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Temporary detention of baggage
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 142. Temporary detention of baggage.- Where the baggage of passenger contains any article which is dutiable or the import of which is prohibited or restricted and in respect of which a true declaration has been made under section 139, the appropriate officer may, at the request of the passenger, detain such article for the purpose of being returned to him on his leaving 1[Bangladesh].

Baggage: If a passenger's baggage contains dutiable, prohibited, or restricted items for which a true declaration has been made, the appropriate officer may detain these items at the passenger's request.
Detained baggage is held for the specific purpose of returning it to the passenger when they leave the country.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is authorized to detain specific articles found within a passenger's baggage if the passenger makes a formal request and has properly declared the goods as required.
Customs Declaration: The ability to detain baggage for return upon a passenger's departure is conditional upon the passenger having made a true declaration of the goods as required by law.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Treatment of baggage of passengers or crew in transit
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 143. Treatment of baggage of passengers or crew in transit.- Baggage of passengers and members of the crew in transit in respect of which a declaration has been made under section 139, may be permitted by the appropriate officer, subject to such limitations, conditions and restrictions as may be specified in the rules, to be so transited without payment of duty.

Passenger or Crew Baggage: Baggage belonging to passengers or crew in transit may be exempted from customs duty provided a proper declaration is filed under the relevant section of the Customs Act.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer is authorized to permit the transit of passenger or crew baggage without the payment of customs duty, subject to specific conditions and restrictions prescribed by the rules.
Baggage Declaration: A formal declaration of passenger or crew baggage must be made under the provisions of the Customs Act for the baggage to be eligible for transit without duty payment.
Rules: The rules define the specific limitations, conditions, and restrictions under which passenger or crew baggage may be allowed to transit through customs jurisdiction without duty.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Label or declaration in respect of goods imported or exported by post to be treated as entry
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 144. Label or declaration in respect of goods imported or exported by post to be treated as entry.- In the case of goods imported or exported by post, any label or declaration which contains the description, quantity and value thereof shall be deemed to be an entry for import or export, as the case may be, for the purposes of this Act.

Imported or Exported Goods: Goods imported or exported through the postal service are subject to specific documentation requirements under the customs law.
A label or declaration accompanying postal goods that lists their description, quantity, and value is legally recognized as a formal entry for import or export purposes.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal basis for treating postal labels or declarations as formal entries for the purposes of customs import and export procedures.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Rate of duty in respect of goods imported or exported by post
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
145. Rate of duty in respect of goods imported or exported by post.- (1) The rate of duty, if any, applicable to any goods imported by post shall be the rate in force on the date on which the postal authorities present to the appropriate officer the declaration or label referred to in section 144 for the purpose of assessing the duty thereon.
(2) The rate of duty, if any, applicable to any goods exported by the post shall be the rate in force on the date on which the exporter delivers such goods to the postal authorities for exportation.

Postal Goods: The customs duty rate applicable to goods imported by post is determined by the rate in effect on the date when the postal authorities submit the required declaration or label to the appropriate customs officer.
For goods exported by post, the applicable customs duty rate is the one in force on the day the exporter delivers the goods to the postal authorities for the purpose of exportation.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is responsible for receiving the postal declaration or label from postal authorities to facilitate the assessment of customs duty on imported goods.
Exporter: The exporter determines the timing for duty assessment on exported postal goods by the date they deliver such goods to the postal authorities.

processed_clauses.metadata_title: CHAPTER XVI PROVISIONS RELATING TO COASTAL GOODS AND VESSELS
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
CHAPTER XVI
PROVISIONS RELATING TO COASTAL GOODS AND VESSELS

Coastal Goods and Vessels Provisions: This chapter of the Customs Act 1969 establishes the legal framework and regulatory requirements governing the movement of goods and the operation of vessels within the coastal waters of Bangladesh.
It provides the foundational authority for customs control over coastal trade and the specific procedures applicable to vessels designated for such transport.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Chapter not to apply to baggage
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 146. Chapter not to apply to baggage.- The provisions of this Chapter shall not apply to baggage.

Baggage: The provisions of the specified chapter of the Customs Act 1969 do not apply to baggage.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Entry of coastal goods
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
147. Entry of coastal goods.- (1) The consignor of any coastal goods shall present to the appropriate officer a bill of coastal goods in the form prescribed by the Board.
(2) Every such consignor shall make a declaration on the bill of coastal goods presented by him as to the truth of the contents thereof.

Coastal Goods: The consignor of coastal goods is required to present a formal bill to the appropriate officer for the entry of such goods.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer is the authority to whom the bill of coastal goods must be presented by the consignor.
Bill of Coastal Goods: This document must be presented by the consignor in the form prescribed by the Board to facilitate the entry of coastal goods.
The consignor is legally obligated to include a declaration on this document confirming the truthfulness of the information provided within it.
National Board of Revenue: The Board holds the authority to prescribe the specific form required for the submission of the bill of coastal goods.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Coastal goods not to be loaded until bill relating thereto is passed
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
148. Coastal goods not to be loaded until bill relating thereto is passed.- No vessel shall take on board any coastal goods until the bill relating to such goods has been passed by the appropriate officer and delivered to the master of the vessel by the consignor:
Provided that the appropriate officer may, in circumstances of exceptional nature, on a written application by the master of the vessel, permit loading of coastal goods pending the presentation and passing of bills relating to such goods.

Coastal Goods: These goods cannot be loaded onto a vessel until the relevant bill has been passed by the appropriate officer and delivered to the vessel master.

In exceptional circumstances, an appropriate officer may authorize the loading of these goods before the required bills are formally presented and passed, provided the vessel master submits a written application.
Coastal Vessel: A vessel is prohibited from taking coastal goods on board until the proper documentation has been processed and delivered to the master.
Bill of Coastal Goods: This document must be passed by the appropriate officer and delivered to the master of the vessel before the loading of coastal goods can commence.
The requirement for this bill to be passed may be waived in exceptional circumstances by the appropriate officer upon a written application from the vessel master.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is responsible for passing the bills relating to coastal goods.
This officer holds the discretionary authority to permit the loading of coastal goods without a pre-passed bill in exceptional cases if the vessel master provides a written request.
Coastal Vessel Master: The master must receive the passed bill from the consignor before coastal goods can be legally loaded onto the vessel.
The master may apply in writing for special permission to load coastal goods if the standard bill passing process cannot be completed.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Clearance of coastal goods at destination
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
149. Clearance of coastal goods at destination.- (1) The master of a vessel carrying any coastal goods shall carry on board the vessel all bills delivered to him under section 148 and shall, within twenty-four hours of arrival of the vessel at any customs-port or coastal port, deliver to the appropriate officer all bills relating to the goods which are to be unloaded at that port.
(2) Where any coastal goods are unloaded at any port, the appropriate officer shall permit their clearance if he is satisfied that they are entered in a bill delivered to him under sub-section (1).

Coastal Vessel Master: The master of a vessel carrying coastal goods is required to carry all bills relating to the goods delivered under Section 148 on board the vessel.
Upon arrival at a customs-port or coastal port, the master must deliver all bills for the goods intended for unloading to the appropriate officer within twenty-four hours.
Coastal Goods: These goods must be covered by bills carried by the vessel master, which are to be submitted to the customs authority upon arrival at the destination port.
The appropriate officer will authorize the clearance of these goods once they are verified against the bills submitted by the vessel master.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer receives the bills for coastal goods from the vessel master upon the vessel's arrival at a customs or coastal port.
The officer has the authority to permit the clearance of coastal goods if they are satisfied that the goods are correctly entered in the submitted bills.
Bill of Coastal Goods: These documents are required to be carried on the vessel and presented to the appropriate officer at the destination port to facilitate the legal unloading and clearance of the goods.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Declaration concerning coasting vessel which has touched foreign post
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 150. Declaration concerning coasting vessel which has touched foreign post.- The master of a vessel carrying coastal goods which has touched at any foreign port immediately before its arrival at a port of 1[Bangladesh] shall deliver, along with the bills referred to in section 149, a declaration stating that fact and indicating the particulars and specifications of the cargo, if any, discharged or taken on board at such foreign port.

Coastal Vessel: The master of a coastal vessel that has stopped at a foreign port prior to arrival at a domestic port is required to provide a formal declaration regarding that stop.
Coastal Goods: When a vessel carrying coastal goods has touched a foreign port, the master must report all details concerning any cargo that was loaded or unloaded at that foreign location.
Master of the Vessel: The master is responsible for submitting a declaration alongside the relevant coastal goods documentation whenever the vessel has visited a foreign port before entering a port in the country.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Cargo book

Cargo Book: A cargo book must be maintained on board every coasting vessel to record critical information about the vessel's journey and transported goods.
The master of the vessel is required to produce the cargo book for inspection upon demand by the appropriate officer of customs, who may annotate it as necessary.
Entries in the cargo book must be made at the specific ports where goods are loaded or discharged.
Coastal Vessel: Every coasting vessel is required to maintain a cargo book that documents the vessel's registration details, the master's name, and comprehensive records of its cargo and voyage details.
Master of the Vessel: It is the duty of the master of every coasting vessel to ensure the cargo book is maintained and updated with details regarding voyage routes, departure and arrival times, and a full account of goods loaded or discharged.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer is authorized to demand the production of the cargo book for inspection and has the authority to record notes or remarks within the document.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Coastal goods not to be loaded or unloaded except at customs-port or coastal port
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 152. Coastal goods not to be loaded or unloaded except at customs- port or coastal port.- No coastal goods shall be loaded on, or unloaded from, any vessel at any port other than a customs-port or a coastal port declared under section 9.

Coastal Goods: Coastal goods are strictly prohibited from being loaded onto or unloaded from any vessel at any location other than a designated customs-port or a coastal port.
Customs Port: This is a legally designated location where the loading and unloading of coastal goods are permitted under the Act.
Coastal Vessel: Coastal vessels must comply with requirements to load or unload goods only at authorized customs-ports or coastal ports.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Coasting vessel to obtain written orders before departure
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
153. Coasting vessel to obtain written orders before departure.- (1) No coasting vessel which has brought or loaded any coastal goods at a customs- port or coastal port shall depart from such port until a written order to that effect has been given by the appropriate officer.
(2) No such order shall be given until -
(a) the master of the vessel has answered the questions, if any, put to him;
(b) all charges and penalties, if any, payable in respect of that vessel or by its master have been paid or the payment secured by such guarantee as the appropriate officer may direct.

Coastal Vessel: A coasting vessel that has loaded or brought coastal goods at a port is prohibited from departing without obtaining a written order from the appropriate officer.
The departure of such vessels is strictly regulated to ensure compliance with customs procedures at the port of departure.
Coastal Goods: The movement of coastal goods triggers a requirement for the vessel to secure a written departure order from the appropriate officer before leaving the port.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is empowered to issue written orders for the departure of coastal vessels.
The officer must ensure that all relevant questions are answered and all charges or penalties are settled or secured by a guarantee before authorizing a vessel's departure.
Coastal Vessel Master: The master of the vessel is responsible for answering questions from the appropriate officer and ensuring that all outstanding charges and penalties are paid or guaranteed before the vessel is permitted to depart.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Application of certain provisions of this Act to coastal goods
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
154. Application of certain provisions of this Act to coastal goods.- (1) Sections 64, 65 and 66 shall, so far as may be, apply to coastal goods as they apply to imported goods or goods for export.
(2) Section 48 and 60 shall, so far as may be, apply to vessels carrying coastal goods as they apply to vessels carrying imported goods or goods for export.
(3) The 1[Government] may, by notification in the official Gazette, direct that all or any of the other provisions of Chapter VII and the provisions of section 78 shall apply to coastal goods or vessels carrying coastal goods with such exceptions and modifications, if any, as may be specified in the notification.

Coastal Goods: The provisions of the Act relating to imported or exported goods, specifically sections 64, 65, and 66, are extended to apply to coastal goods. The Government may also extend additional provisions from Chapter VII and section 78 to these goods, subject to any exceptions or modifications specified in a notification.
Vessels Carrying Coastal Goods: The provisions of the Act governing vessels that carry imported or exported goods, specifically sections 48 and 60, are extended to apply to vessels carrying coastal goods. The Government has the authority to apply further regulatory provisions of the Act to these vessels through an official gazette notification.
Government: The Government is empowered to issue official notifications to extend specific provisions of Chapter VII and section 78 of the Act to coastal goods or vessels carrying coastal goods, potentially including specific modifications or exceptions.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Prohibition of the coastal trade of certain goods
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 155. Prohibition of the coastal trade of certain goods.- No goods shall be carried coastwise or shipped as stores in a coasting vessel contrary to any prohibition or restriction imposed by or under any law, nor shall such goods or stores be brought to any place in 1[Bangladesh] for the purpose of being so carried or shipped.

Coastal Trade: The transport of goods by sea between coastal points is subject to strict prohibition or restriction as mandated by law.
Goods or stores intended for coastal transport are prohibited from being brought to any location in Bangladesh if their movement violates existing legal restrictions.
Coastal Vessel: A vessel engaged in the movement of goods coastwise must comply with all legal prohibitions and restrictions regarding the carriage or shipment of specific items.
Goods: Goods are prohibited from being shipped or carried coastwise if such action contravenes any legal restriction.
The law prevents the movement or storage of restricted goods for the purpose of coastal shipping.

OFFENCES AND PENALTIES

Customs Offence Penalties: This chapter outlines the legal framework and provisions governing various offences related to customs law and the corresponding penalties applicable to such violations.
