Bill of Export: The inspection of export goods by the owner or their representative must occur before the presentation or transmission of the bill of export.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to take sample of goods
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
199. Power to take sample of goods.- (1) The appropriate officer may, on the entry or clearance of any goods or at any time while such goods are being passed through the customs-area, take samples of such goods in the presence of the owner thereof or his agent, for examination or testing or for ascertaining the value thereof or for any other necessary purpose.

(2) After the purpose for which a sample was taken in carried out, such sample shall, if practicable, be restored to the owner, but if the owner fails to take delivery of the sample within one month of the date on which he is asked in writing to take its delivery, it may be disposed of in such manner as the 2[Commissioner of Customs] may direct.

(3) In the case of goods which consist of drugs or articles intended for consumption as food, and in respect of which the taking of samples for the purposes of this sub-section may have been authorised by a general or special order of the 3[Government], the appropriate officer may also in like circumstances take samples thereof for submission to, and examination by such officer of Government or of a local authority as may be specified in such order.

4[(4) The owner of any imported or exportable goods or his authorized representative may draw samples before presentation or transmission of bill of entry or bill of export thereof, as the case may be, subject to the conditions laid down by an officer of customs not below the rank of Assistant Commissioner.]

Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer has the authority to collect samples of goods during their entry, clearance, or transit through the customs-area for the purposes of examination, testing, valuation, or other necessary official actions.
When collecting samples, the officer must ensure the presence of the owner or their agent.
In the case of food or drug items, the officer may collect samples for examination by specified government or local authority officials if authorized by a general or special government order.
Agent: The agent of the owner of the goods is required to be present when samples are being drawn by the appropriate officer of customs.
Goods: Samples of goods may be drawn for testing, examination, or valuation during the customs clearance process or while within the customs-area.
Once the purpose for testing or examination is fulfilled, samples should be returned to the owner if it is practicable to do so.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to direct the disposal of samples if the owner fails to collect them within one month of receiving a written request to do so.
Government: The government may issue general or special orders authorizing the collection of samples for food or drug products to be examined by specific authorities.
Imported or Exported Goods: Owners or their authorized representatives may request to draw samples of goods prior to the formal submission of a bill of entry or bill of export, provided they meet the conditions specified by a customs officer at or above the rank of Assistant Commissioner of Customs.
Authorized Representative: An authorized representative is permitted to draw samples of goods before the formal filing of entry or export documents under specific conditions established by an Assistant Commissioner of Customs or a higher-ranking officer.
Assistant Commissioner of Customs: An Assistant Commissioner of Customs or any officer of higher rank holds the authority to set the conditions under which an owner or authorized representative may draw samples of goods prior to the filing of a bill of entry or bill of export.
Bill of Entry: The owner or authorized representative may draw samples of imported goods before the presentation of the bill of entry, subject to compliance with conditions set by a senior customs officer.
Bill of Export: The owner or authorized representative may draw samples of export goods before the transmission of the bill of export, subject to compliance with conditions set by a senior customs officer.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Owner to make all arrangements and bear all expenses
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 200. Owner to make all arrangements and bear all expenses.- Any opening, un-packing, waiving, measuring, re-packing, bulking, sorting, letting, marking numbering, loading, unloading, carrying or lading of goods or their containers for the purposes of, or incidental to, the 5[examination, including any investigation, scientific or chemical test or draft survey, by an officer of Customs, removal or warehousing thereof shall be done, and any facilities or assistance required for any such examination, investigation, test or survey shall be provided, by or at the expense of the owner of goods].

Goods: The owner of the goods is responsible for all arrangements and costs associated with the handling, processing, and preparation of goods for customs examination or warehousing purposes.
Customs Examination of Goods: The owner must facilitate any required examination, investigation, scientific or chemical test, or draft survey conducted by an officer of customs at their own expense.
Container: The owner is responsible for all costs and logistical arrangements associated with the handling of containers during customs-related processes such as loading, unloading, and examination.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Procedure for sale of goods and application of sale proceeds

Customs Goods Sale: The procedure for selling non-confiscated goods under this Act involves notifying the owner and selling the goods via public auction, tender, private offer, or other mutually agreed-upon methods.

The proceeds from the sale of goods must be distributed in a specific order: first to cover sale expenses, then to settle freight or other service charges, followed by payment of customs duties and taxes to the Government, and finally to pay custody charges to the relevant party.
Sale Proceeds Disbursement: Any remaining balance from the sale proceeds after all statutory debts, taxes, and service fees are paid is to be disbursed to the owner of the goods.
The owner of the goods is entitled to claim the balance of the sale proceeds, provided they submit an application within the prescribed time limit following the sale.
Government: The Government is entitled to receive payment for customs duties, taxes, and other dues incurred by the goods prior to the disbursement of any surplus funds to the owner.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Recovery of Government dues

Customs Act 1969: This act establishes the legal framework for the recovery of government dues including duties, regulatory duties, and penalties.
It empowers customs authorities to employ various mechanisms, including detention, sale of goods, and certificate proceedings, to recover outstanding amounts owed to the government.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The officer is authorized to enforce the recovery of unpaid dues by deducting amounts from funds held by the government, stopping the clearance of goods, or issuing notices to third parties holding money for the defaulter.
The officer can initiate formal recovery procedures by preparing a certificate for unpaid dues and referring the matter for collection as a public demand or land revenue.
Customs Duty: Customs duty is a government due that must be paid within the prescribed timeframe or ordered period to avoid the initiation of recovery proceedings.
Regulatory Duty: Regulatory duty is classified as a government due subject to the same recovery enforcement provisions as other customs duties under the act.
Customs Station: Customs-stations are locations where the clearance of goods belonging to a defaulter can be suspended until all government dues are paid in full.
Bonded Warehouse: The authorities may suspend the clearance of goods from a bonded warehouse to recover unpaid government dues owed by a person.
Value Added Tax: The Value Added Tax officer is empowered to recover government dues through the attachment and sale of goods or equipment from a factory or warehouse belonging to the person liable for the payment.
Scheduled Bank: A Scheduled Bank may be required by a written notice to freeze or render inoperative the account of a person who has failed to pay government dues.
Public Demands Recovery Act 1913: This act serves as the legal basis for the appointment of certificate officers tasked with recovering outstanding government dues as a public demand or arrear of land revenue.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to write off sums due to Government
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 5[202A. Power to write off sums due to Government.- When under this Act or the rules made thereunder a duty or any other money is payable to the Government by any person or a penalty is adjudged against any person and such duty, penalty or other sum has not been paid within the time it was required to be paid and the sum could not be recovered nor is recoverable from such person in the manner provided in section 202 due to bankruptcy or untraceability of such person or for any other reason, the Government may write-off such duty, penalty or other sum, wholly or partially as it deems fit in the manner prescribed by rules.]

Government: The Government is empowered to write off, in whole or in part, outstanding duties, penalties, or other sums due from a person if recovery has failed due to bankruptcy, the person being untraceable, or other sufficient reasons.
The process for exercising this power to write off sums must be carried out in the manner prescribed by rules.
Customs Duty: This entity is identified as a sum payable to the Government that may be written off under the prescribed conditions when recovery efforts have been unsuccessful.
Customs Penalty: A penalty adjudged against a person under the Act or rules that remains unpaid and unrecoverable may be subject to being written off by the Government.
Rules: The procedures for the Government to perform a write-off of outstanding duties or penalties must be established and followed in accordance with the rules.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Wharfage or storage fees
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 203. Wharfage or storage fees.- The 6[Commissioner of Customs] may, from time to time, fix the period after the expiration of which goods left 7[or detained] in any custom-house, customs-area, wharf of other authorised landing place or part of the custom-house premises, shall be subject to payment of fees, and the amount of such fees.

Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs is empowered to set the time limit after which goods remaining at customs locations become subject to fees.
The Commissioner of Customs has the authority to determine the specific rate or amount of wharfage or storage fees applicable to goods left or detained in authorized customs areas.
Wharfage or Storage Fees: These fees are imposed on goods that remain at a custom-house, customs-area, wharf, or other authorized landing place beyond a period specified by the Commissioner of Customs.
The application of these fees is triggered once the time limit for leaving or detaining goods in customs premises has expired.
Goods: Goods left or detained in a custom-house, customs-area, wharf, or other authorized landing place are subject to the payment of wharfage or storage fees once a specific time period has elapsed.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Issue of certificate and duplicates of customs' document
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 204. Issue of certificate and duplicates of customs' document.- A certificate or a duplicate of any certificate, manifest, bill or other customs' document may, 43[on payment of such fee as the Board may determine for this purpose], be furnished, at the discretion of an officer of customs not below the rank of an 10[Assistant Commissioner of Customs], to any person applying for the same, if the said officer is satisfied that no fraud has been committed or is intended to be committed by the applicant.

Customs Documents: A person may apply for and be issued a certificate or a duplicate of any certificate, manifest, bill, or other customs document.
The issuance of these documents is subject to the payment of a fee determined by the National Board of Revenue and is at the discretion of an authorized officer.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to determine the fees applicable for the issuance of customs certificates and duplicate documents.
Assistant Commissioner of Customs: This officer or any customs official of a higher rank has the discretionary authority to issue requested certificates or duplicate documents.
Officer of Customs: The officer must be satisfied that the applicant has not committed and does not intend to commit any fraud before approving the issuance of the requested customs documents.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Supply of information pertaining to customs law, etc
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 1[204A. Supply of information pertaining to customs law, etc.- On an application by any interested person the Board may, within a reasonable period and on payment of such fee as the Board may determine for this purpose, provide him with information pertaining to including in electronic form of uptodate Customs Laws including Rules, notifications, circulars, orders and other instruments issued for general use under this Act.]

National Board of Revenue: The Board is authorized to receive applications from interested persons seeking access to customs-related information.
The Board holds the power to determine the fees required for providing such information and must provide the requested materials within a reasonable time frame.
Customs Information Access: Interested persons may apply to obtain updated information regarding customs laws, including rules, notifications, circulars, and other orders issued under the Customs Act.
This information may be provided in various formats, including electronic versions, to ensure transparency and accessibility.
Customs Act 1969: This Act serves as the legal foundation for the issuance of rules, notifications, and circulars that are subject to information disclosure requests under this section.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Amendment of documents
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 44[205. Amendment of documents.- Except in the case provided for by sections 29, 45, 53 and 88, an officer of customs not below the rank of an Assistant Commissioner of Customs may, in his discretion, on payment of such fee as the Board may determined for this purpose, authorize any document, after it has been presented at the customs house, to be amended.]

Document Amendment: The law allows for the amendment of customs documents after they have been presented at a customs house, provided specific conditions are met. This process is subject to the discretion of an authorized customs officer and the payment of a prescribed fee.
Assistant Commissioner of Customs: An officer of this rank or higher is empowered to authorize the amendment of customs documents at their discretion, provided the required fee has been paid.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is responsible for determining the fee required for the amendment of customs documents.
Customs House: This is the official location where documents must be presented before they can be considered for amendment under the specified legal provisions.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Correction of clerical errors, etc
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 206. Correction of clerical errors, etc.- Clerical or arithmetical errors in any decision or order passed by the 5[Government], the Board or any officer of customs under this Act, or errors arising therein from accidental slip or omission may, at any time, be corrected by the 8[Government], the Board or such officer of customs or his successor in office, as the case may be.

Customs Decision: This clause provides a mechanism for the correction of clerical or arithmetical errors within any decision or order made under the Customs Act.
Corrections for errors resulting from accidental slips or omissions can be made at any time.
Government: The Government has the authority to rectify clerical or arithmetical errors in its own orders or decisions, or those of its successors, under the Act.
National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to correct clerical or arithmetical mistakes, or errors arising from accidental slips or omissions, in any of its issued orders or decisions.
Officer of Customs: An Officer of Customs is authorized to correct clerical or arithmetical errors in their own decisions or orders, or those made by their predecessors in office.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Custom-house agents to be licensed
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 207. Custom-house agents to be licensed.- No person shall act as an agent for the transaction of any business relating to the entrance or departure of any conveyance or the import or export of goods or baggage at any customs-station unless such person holds a licence granted in this behalf in accordance with the rules.

Customs House Agent: No individual or entity may act as an agent for transactions regarding the entrance or departure of conveyances, or the import or export of goods or baggage at a customs station, without holding a valid licence. The issuance of such a licence must be conducted in accordance with the rules established under the Act.
Customs Station: This location serves as the jurisdictional point where agents are required to hold a licence to transact business related to the movement of conveyances, goods, or baggage.
Conveyance: Agents must be licensed to handle any business pertaining to the entrance or departure of these vessels or vehicles at a customs station.
Goods: The import or export of these items at a customs station requires the services of a duly licensed customs house agent.
Baggage: The import or export of this category of items at a customs station is subject to the requirement that the agent involved must hold a valid licence.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Agent to produce authority if required
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
208. Agent to produce authority if required.- (1) When any person applies to any officer of customs for permission to transact any specified business with him on behalf of any other person, such officer may require the applicant to produce a written authority from the person on whose behalf such business is to be transacted, and in default of the production of such authority refuse such permission.(2) The clerk, servant or agent of any person or mercantile firm may transact business generally at the customs-house on behalf of such person or firm :

Provided that the appropriate officer may refuse to recognize such clerk, servant or agent unless such person or a member of such firm identifies such clerk, servant or agent to the appropriate officer as empowered to transact such business, and deposits with the said officer an authority in writing duly signed, authorising such clerk, servant or agent to transact such business on behalf of such person or firm.

Agent: An agent acting on behalf of a person or mercantile firm may transact business at a custom-house.
The appropriate officer of customs may require an agent to produce formal written authorization signed by the person or firm they represent.
An officer may refuse to recognize an agent if they fail to provide the required written authorization or fail to be identified by their principal as empowered to conduct business.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: The appropriate officer of customs is empowered to demand written evidence of authority from any person applying to transact business on behalf of another party.
The officer may refuse to grant permission for business transactions if the requested proof of authority is not produced.
The officer has the discretion to refuse to recognize an agent, servant, or clerk unless they have been properly identified by the principal and provided with a signed written authorization.
Customs House: The custom-house serves as the location where authorized agents, clerks, or servants may conduct business on behalf of mercantile firms or individuals.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Liability of principal and agent
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
209. Liability of principal and agent.- (1) Subject to the provisions of sections 207 and 208, anything which the owner of any goods is required or empowered to do under this Act may be done by any person expressly or impliedly authorised by the owner for the purpose.

(2) Where this Act requires anything to be done by the owner, importer or exporter of any goods, any such thing done by an agent, clerk or servant of the owner, importer or exporter of any goods shall, unless the contrary is proved, be deemed to have been done with the knowledge and consent of such owner, importer or exporter so that in any proceedings under this Act, the owner, importer or exporter of the goods shall also be liable as if the thing had been done by himself.

(3) When any person is expressly or impliedly authorised by the owner, importer or exporter of any goods to be his agent in respect of such goods for all or any of the purposes of this Act, such person shall, without prejudice to the liability of the owner, importer or exporter, be deemed to be the owner, importer or exporter of such goods for such purposes:

Provided that where any duty is not levied or is short-levied or erroneously refunded on account of any reason other than wilful act, negligence or default of the agent, such duty shall not be recovered from the agent.

Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of goods may perform any act required or empowered under the Customs Act 1969 through an authorized person, subject to specific legal conditions.
Importer: When an importer is required to perform specific actions under the Customs Act 1969, acts performed by their agent, clerk, or servant are legally deemed to be performed with the importer's knowledge and consent.
An importer remains liable for actions performed by their authorized agent during customs proceedings as if the importer had performed the action personally.
Exporter: Acts performed by an agent, clerk, or servant of an exporter are legally attributed to the exporter, making the exporter liable for such actions in customs proceedings unless proven otherwise.
An authorized agent acting on behalf of an exporter is deemed to be the exporter for the purposes of the Act, though this does not absolve the actual exporter of their own liability.
Agent: An agent authorized by an owner, importer, or exporter can perform duties under the Customs Act 1969, and their actions are legally binding on their principal.
An agent is deemed to be the owner, importer, or exporter for the purposes of the Act when authorized to act in that capacity.
Agents are protected from liability for unlevied, short-levied, or erroneously refunded duties if such occurrences were not caused by the agent's wilful act, negligence, or default.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Liability of agent appointment by the person-in-charge of a conveyance
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
210. Liability of agent appointment by the person-in-charge of a conveyance.- (1) Anything which the person-in-charge of a conveyance is required or empowered to do under this Act may, with the express or implied consent of the person-in-charge and the approval of the appropriate officer, be done by his agent.

(2) An agent appointed by the person-in-charge of a conveyance, and any person who represents himself to any officer of customs as an agent of any such person-in-charge and is accepted as such by that officer, shall be liable for the fulfilment in respect of the matter in question of all obligations imposed on such person-in-charge by or under this Act or any law for the time being in force, and to penalties ( including confiscation) which may be incurred in respect of that matter.

Person in Charge of Conveyance: The person in charge of a conveyance is permitted to authorize an agent to perform actions required or empowered under the Customs Act.
They retain ultimate responsibility for obligations and liabilities, but may delegate the performance of these duties with the approval of an appropriate customs officer.
Agent: An agent may act on behalf of the person in charge of a conveyance provided they have the express or implied consent of the person in charge and approval from an appropriate officer.
An agent, or anyone representing themselves as an agent and accepted by an officer, assumes full legal liability for all obligations imposed on the person in charge of the conveyance.
Agents are subject to all penalties, including the confiscation of goods or vehicles, related to the matters they handle for the person in charge.
Appropriate Officer of Customs: This officer is empowered to approve the appointment of an agent acting on behalf of the person in charge of a conveyance.
They have the authority to formally accept a person who represents themselves as an agent, thereby binding that person to the legal obligations and liabilities of the person in charge.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Keeping of business record
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
1[211. Keeping of business record.- 2[(1)] Every licensee, importer, exporter or their agents shall keep or cause to be kept such records as may be specified by the Board, for a period of three years.]
(2) Every such person must, as and when required by an officer of Customs.-
(a) make the records and accounts available to Customs;
(b) provide copies of the records and accounts as required; and
(c) answer any question relevant to the matters arising under this Act asked by any officer of Customs in respect of them.
(3) Where for the purpose of complying with sub-section (2) of this section, information is recorded or stored by means of an electronic or other device, the licensee, importer, exporter, or its agent, shall, at the request of an officer of Customs, operate the device, or cause it to be operated, to fulfil the requirements of sub-sections (2).]
3[(4) For the purposes of sub-section (2) and (3) the audit agencies appointed by the Government under section 25A and an employee of that agency shall be deemed to be the officers of Customs.]

Licensee: Licensees are required to maintain business records specified by the National Board of Revenue for a duration of three years.
They must provide these records, facilitate access to accounts, and respond to inquiries from customs officials as necessary.
When data is stored electronically, licensees must operate or facilitate the operation of relevant devices to ensure customs access to that information.
Importer: Importers must maintain business records as directed by the National Board of Revenue for a period of three years.
They are obligated to provide copies of records and answer questions from customs officers regarding their business activities.
Importers must provide access to electronic or stored data upon request by a customs officer to ensure compliance with record-keeping obligations.
Exporter: Exporters are mandated to keep records specified by the National Board of Revenue for at least three years.
Exporters must allow customs officers to examine their records and answer any questions relating to their export business.
Exporters are required to operate or provide access to electronic record-keeping devices when requested by an officer of Customs.
Agent: Agents acting on behalf of licensees, importers, or exporters share the responsibility to keep prescribed business records for three years.
They are required to facilitate customs access to accounts and respond to official queries regarding these records.
Agents must operate electronic systems or devices to provide customs officers with the necessary information and records when requested.
National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue holds the authority to specify the types of business records that must be kept by licensees, importers, exporters, and their agents.
Officer of Customs: Officers of Customs are empowered to require the production of business records, the provision of copies, and the answering of relevant questions by regulated persons.
They have the authority to request that electronic record-keeping devices be operated to retrieve information for official inspection.
Audit Agency: Audit agencies appointed by the Government under the Customs Act are legally deemed to be officers of Customs when performing their duties related to the verification of records and accounts.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Regulation of business of gold, etc
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 212. Regulation of business of gold, etc.- The 4[Government] may, by notification in the official Gazette, regulate business in, or connected with, gold or silver or precious stones or ornaments made of gold or silver or precious stones, within fifteen miles of the frontier or cost-line of 1[Bangladesh].

Government: The Government is empowered to regulate business activities concerning gold, silver, precious stones, or their ornaments within a specified distance from the frontier or coastline.
Trade of Gold and Precious Metals: Business activities involving gold, silver, precious stones, or ornaments made of these materials that occur within a specified distance from the frontier or coastline are subject to government regulation through official notification.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Recovery of money upon certain documents
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 213. Recovery of money upon certain documents.- If any person knowingly makes or brings into 1[Bangladesh] or causes or authorises or is otherwise concerned in the making or bringing into 1[Bangladesh] of any invoice or paper used or intended to be used as an invoice for the purposes of customs, in which any goods are entered or charged at a price or value higher or lower than that actually paid or intended to be paid for them, or in which goods are falsely described, no sum of money shall be recoverable by such person, his representatives or assigns, for the price of such goods or any part thereof, nor shall any sum of money be recoverable upon any bill of exchange, note or other security made, given or executed for the whole or part of the price of such goods unless such bill of exchange, note or other security is in the hands of a bona fide holder for consideration without notice.

Customs Invoice and Documentation: It is illegal to knowingly create, import, or authorize the use of customs invoices that state a value different from the actual price paid or that describe goods falsely.
Persons involved in the creation or use of such fraudulent documents are prohibited from recovering any payments for the price of the goods involved.
Bill of Exchange and Financial Security: Money cannot be recovered based on any financial security, note, or bill of exchange related to goods for which false customs documentation was produced.
The only exception is if the security is held by a bona fide holder who provided consideration and had no prior knowledge of the fraudulent nature of the underlying transaction.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Remission of duty and payment of compensation to the owner in certain cases
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 214. Remission of duty and payment of compensation to the owner in certain cases.- Where, on prosecution by the owner of any goods, an officer of customs is convicted of an offence connected with the removal of such goods from the warehouse without payment of duty, the whole of the duty on such goods shall be remitted, and, the 2[Commissioner of Customs] shall, in accordance with the rules, pay to the owner due compensation for the damage caused to the owner by such offence.

Goods: In the event of an officer of customs being convicted for illegally removing goods from a warehouse without duty payment, the total customs duty applicable to such goods is remitted.
Officer of Customs: If an officer of customs is convicted of an offence involving the unauthorized removal of warehoused goods without duty payment, specific legal consequences regarding duty remission and compensation are triggered.
Commissioner of Customs: Following a conviction of a customs officer for the unauthorized removal of goods, the Commissioner of Customs is legally obligated to pay compensation to the owner of the goods as prescribed by the rules.
Owner of Warehoused Goods: The owner of goods is entitled to have the applicable duty remitted and receive compensation from the Commissioner of Customs if their goods were illegally removed from a warehouse by a customs officer who is subsequently convicted for the act.
Warehouse: The provisions apply specifically to goods stored in a warehouse, addressing cases where an officer of customs unlawfully removes such goods without payment of duty.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Service of order, decision, etc
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
215. Service of order, decision, etc.- Any order or decision passed or any summons or notice issued under this Act shall be served-
(a) by tendering the order, decision, summons or notice or sending it by registered post acknowledgement due to the person for whom it is intended or to his agent; or
(b) if the order, decision, summons or notice cannot be served in any manner provided in clause (a), by affixing it on the notice board of the customs-house.

Customs Decision: Any order, decision, summons, or notice issued under the Customs Act 1969 must be served either by registered post to the intended person or their agent, or by being affixed to the customs-house notice board if personal service is not possible.
Summons Mechanism: Provisions are established for the formal service of summons to the intended recipient or their authorized agent, including requirements for alternative service methods via public notice.
Agent: Service of orders, decisions, summons, or notices may be legally effected by delivering the document to the agent of the person for whom the communication is intended.
Customs House: If a legal document or notice cannot be served directly to the relevant person or their agent, it may be validly served by affixing it to the notice board located at the custom-house.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Supply of information and copy of decisions
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
3[215A. Supply of information and copy of decisions.- (1) Upon an application of a person directly interested in a decision taken by a customs officer under this Act, the Commissioner of Customs or an officer authorised by him shall, subject to payment by the applicant of a fee specified by the Board, deliver within 15 (fifteen) days of the application, a true copy of that decision with a certificate that it is a true copy :

Provided that a copy or other copy or reproduction of the certified copy shall not be admissible as evidence or otherwise accepted in any court of law.

(2) Upon an application of a person directly interested in a decision taken or omitted to have been taken by a customs officer, the Commissioner of Customs shall inform that person in writing within a period of 60 days of the application the reasons for such decision or omission.]

Customs Decision: A person directly interested in a decision taken by a customs officer has the right to obtain a certified true copy of that decision upon application and payment of the prescribed fee.

A person directly interested in a decision or omission by a customs officer has the right to receive a written explanation of the reasons for such action or inaction from the Commissioner of Customs within a specified period.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs or an authorized officer is responsible for providing a certified true copy of a customs decision to an interested applicant within a defined timeframe upon payment of the specified fee.
The Commissioner of Customs is mandated to provide a written explanation for a decision or omission to an interested applicant within the stipulated time limit.
Documentary Evidence: Any copy or reproduction of a certified true copy of a customs decision is explicitly declared inadmissible as evidence in any court of law.
National Board of Revenue: The Board has the authority to specify the fee payable by an applicant for obtaining a certified true copy of a customs decision.

processed_clauses.clause_title: No compensation for loss or injury except on proof of neglect or wilful act
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 216. No compensation for loss or injury except on proof of neglect or wilful act.- No owner of goods shall be entitled to claim from any officer of customs compensation for the loss of such goods or for damage done to them at any time while they remain or are lawfully detained in any customs-house, customs-area, wharf or landing place under the charge of any officer of customs, unless it be proved that such loss or damage was occasioned by gross negligence or wilful act of such officer.

Goods: The owner of goods is restricted from claiming compensation for loss or damage occurring while the goods are held in official customs facilities unless specific conditions regarding officer conduct are met.
Officer of Customs: An officer of customs is not liable to pay compensation for the loss or damage of goods under their charge unless it is proven that such loss or damage resulted from the officer's gross negligence or wilful act.
Customs House: This location is designated as a place where goods may be lawfully detained, and the liability of customs officers for damages to goods in this area is strictly limited to cases of proven negligence or wilful misconduct.
Customs-area: This area is designated as a place where goods may be lawfully detained, and the liability of customs officers for damages to goods in this area is strictly limited to cases of proven negligence or wilful misconduct.
Wharf: This infrastructure is identified as a site of lawful detention for goods, where officers are only liable for damage if proven to have acted with gross negligence or intent.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Bar to filing of cases in civil courts
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 1[216A. Bar to filing of cases in civil courts.- No suit, case or any application shall lie to any civil court, except the courts, tribunals and authorities authorized by or under this Act, for the purpose of determination of the legality or propriety of an order or decision, as the case may be, regarding levy, imposition, exemption, assessment or realisation of customs duties or taxes made by an officer of customs or by the Board or the Government.]

Civil Court: The jurisdiction of civil courts is barred in matters concerning the determination of the legality or propriety of orders or decisions related to customs duties and taxes.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the exclusive legal framework for customs disputes, restricting legal challenges to authorized courts, tribunals, and authorities established under its provisions.
Customs Duty: The Act prohibits civil litigation regarding the levy, imposition, exemption, assessment, or realization of customs duties and taxes.
Officer of Customs: Orders or decisions made by an officer of customs regarding the assessment or collection of duties and taxes are excluded from the jurisdiction of civil courts.
National Board of Revenue: Decisions made by the Board concerning the assessment or collection of customs duties are shielded from review by civil courts.
Government: Orders and decisions issued by the Government regarding customs duties and taxes are not subject to challenge in civil courts.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Protection of action taken under the Act
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 217. Protection of action taken under the Act.- No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the 2[Government] or any public servant for anything which is done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of this Act or the rules.

Government: The Government is protected from any suit, prosecution, or legal proceeding for actions taken or intended to be taken in good faith under the provisions of the Customs Act 1969 or associated rules.
Customs Legal Proceedings: This clause provides legal immunity by restricting the filing of suits or prosecutions against the Government or public servants for actions performed in good faith pursuant to the Customs Act 1969 or its rules.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal foundation for the protection of actions taken by public servants and the Government when such actions are performed in good faith.
Rules: Actions taken in good faith under the authority of the rules made pursuant to the Customs Act 1969 are protected from legal proceedings.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Reward for detection etc. of evasion of duties or violation of laws
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
3[217A. Reward for detection etc. of evasion of duties or violation of laws.- Notwithstanding anything contained to the contrary in this Act or any other law for time being in force, the Board may, in such manner and in such circumstances and to such extent as may be prescribed by rules, grant reward to the following persons :-
(a) a person giving information to Customs Authorities with regard to evasion or attempted evasion of customs duties or violation of any provision of this Act or any other law for the time being in force under which a customs officer is authorised to collect tax or other revenue;
(b) 45[an officer or employee of Customs] or an officer or employee of any other government agency or of a local authority who detects or unearths the evasion or attempted evasion of customs duties or violation of this Act or that other law;

if such supply of information, the act of detection of or unearthing the evasion or attempted evasion of customs duty or violation of law leads to :-
(i) the seizure and confiscation of goods or other things in relation to which the evasion or attempted evasion or violation takes place; or
(ii) the realisation of customs duty or other revenue leviable under this Act or that other law for the time being in force or the realisation of a penalty or fine imposed under the relevant law; or
(iii) conviction of and sentence imposed on the person liable for such evasion, attempted evasion or violation.]

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is empowered to grant rewards to eligible persons for the detection of customs duty evasion or legal violations, subject to the procedures and circumstances prescribed by rules.
Person: A person who provides information regarding the evasion of customs duties or violations of relevant customs laws to customs authorities is eligible to receive a reward.
Customs Officer and Employee: Officers or employees of the customs department who detect or unearth the evasion of customs duties or other legal violations are eligible to be granted rewards.
Government Revenue Collection: Rewards may be granted when information or detection leads to the successful realization of customs duties, other government revenues, or the recovery of penalties and fines.
Seizure of Goods: The seizure and subsequent confiscation of goods related to duty evasion or legal violations serve as a condition upon which rewards can be granted to the reporting or detecting party.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Award of financial incentives to Customs Officers and employees
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
46[217B. Award of financial incentives to Customs Officers and employees - Notwithstanding anything contained to the contrary in this Act or any other law the Board may, in such manner and in such circumstances and to such extent as may be prescribed by rules, award an amount of the surplus collection of revenue at import stage as financial incentives to all Customs Officers and employees and officers and employees of the Board;

Provided that the collection of revenue at import stage for a given financial year exceeds the target of collection fixed by the Government for that financial year.]

National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to award financial incentives to customs and board personnel from surplus revenue collections at the import stage.
The manner, circumstances, and extent of these financial awards are subject to rules prescribed by the Board.
Customs Officer: Customs Officers are eligible to receive financial incentives derived from surplus import stage revenue collections, subject to conditions prescribed by rules.
Government Revenue Collection: Financial incentives for customs and board personnel are conditional upon the actual revenue collection at the import stage exceeding the target fixed by the Government for the relevant financial year.
Rules: These rules serve as the regulatory framework that governs the manner, circumstances, and extent under which financial incentives are awarded to customs and board employees.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Notice of proceedings
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 218. Notice of proceedings.- No proceeding in a court other than a suit shall be commenced against any officer of customs or any other person exercising any powers conferred or discharging any duties imposed by or under this Act for anything purporting to be done in pursuance of the provisions of this Act or the rules without giving to such officer or person a months previous notice in writing of the intended proceeding and of the cause thereof; or after the expiration of one year from the actual of such cause.

Customs Legal Proceedings: This clause sets specific procedural requirements for initiating legal actions against customs officials and authorized persons.
A mandatory written notice must be provided at least one month before starting any proceeding, and such actions must be filed within one year of the cause of action.
Officer of Customs: These officials are protected by a mandatory notice period before any legal proceedings can be initiated against them for actions taken in the discharge of their duties under the law.
Person: Any person exercising powers or discharging duties under the Customs Act is entitled to the same procedural protections regarding legal notices as customs officers.
Customs Act 1969: This Act provides the legal foundation for the protection of officials and authorized persons against whom legal proceedings might be brought for actions taken in good faith under its provisions.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to make rules
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
219. Power to make rules.- (1) The Board may, by notification in the official Gazette, make rules for carrying out the purposes of this Act.
(2) Without prejudice to the generality of the foregoing provision, rules may be made on matters enumerated in the 1[Third Schedule].
(3) No rules relating to matters enumerated at items 19 and 22 of the 1[Third Schedule] shall be made without previous approval of the 2[Government] in writing.
(4) All rules made under this section shall, as soon as may be, be laid at the table of the 3[Parliament].
(5) All such rules for the time being in force shall be collected, arranged, and published at intervals not exceeding two years, and shall be sold to the public at a reasonable price.

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is empowered to issue rules through notification in the official Gazette to facilitate the implementation of the provisions of the Customs Act 1969.
The Board is responsible for collecting, arranging, and publishing all active rules every two years and ensuring they are made available for purchase by the public at a reasonable price.
Rules: Rules are subordinate instruments created to carry out the purposes of the Customs Act 1969 and must be laid before Parliament as soon as possible after their issuance.
Specific rules pertaining to matters listed under designated items in the Third Schedule require prior written approval from the Government before they can be enacted.
Third Schedule: The Third Schedule serves as the foundational list of matters for which the National Board of Revenue may prescribe rules.
Items numbered 19 and 22 within the Third Schedule are subject to a mandatory requirement of prior written approval from the Government before any related rules can be issued.
Government: The Government provides the necessary written approval required for the issuance of rules concerning specific sensitive matters identified in the Third Schedule.
Parliament: Parliament serves as the legislative body before which all rules created under the authority of this Act must be laid for oversight.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to make customs rulings
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
4[219A. Power to make customs rulings.- (1) On an application by any person or on a reference by an officer of customs not below the rank of Commissioner or of its own motion, the Board may make customs rulings in respect of any matter specified in the application or reference, as the case may be, if the point raised in the application or reference relates to application of any provision of this Act or the rules to a specific situation or if such point relates to any tariff classification or duty rates or valuation of any goods for customs assessment purpose.
(2) A customs ruling may be made within thirty working days of the receipt of the application or the reference, as the case may be.
(3) The Board may decline to make a customs ruling on the ground of insufficient information furnished or in the absence of conclusive evidence provided in support of the contentions in the application or the reference.
(4) The rulings made by the Board shall be binding upon the concerned persons and officers.
(5) The Board may from time to time review and amend a customs ruling to correct any error contained in that ruling.]

National Board of Revenue: The Board is empowered to issue customs rulings upon request by a person, a reference from a senior customs officer, or on its own motion.
The Board may decline to issue a ruling if the provided information or evidence is insufficient to support the contentions.
The Board has the authority to review and amend existing customs rulings to rectify any errors.
Customs Ruling: A customs ruling may address matters related to the application of customs laws and rules, tariff classification, duty rates, or the valuation of goods.
A ruling must be issued within a specified timeframe after the receipt of the relevant application or reference.
Once issued, customs rulings are legally binding on both the concerned persons and the relevant customs officers.
Person: Any person may submit an application to the Board to obtain a formal customs ruling regarding a specific situation.
Officer of Customs: Officers of customs at or above the rank of Commissioner may make a reference to the Board for the issuance of a customs ruling.
Customs officers are bound by the customs rulings issued by the Board.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Power to issue Orders, Notices, Explanations or Circulars
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 5[219B. Power to issue Orders, Notices, Explanations or Circulars.- The Board or, as the case may be, the Commissioner of Customs (Bond), or Commissioner of Customs (Valuation and internal audit), or any other Commissioner of Customs or any Director General may issue orders, notices, explanations or circulars within their respective jurisdiction not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder.]

National Board of Revenue: The National Board of Revenue is empowered to issue orders, notices, explanations, or circulars that are consistent with the provisions of the Customs Act and its subordinate rules.
Commissioner of Customs: The Commissioner of Customs (Bond) is authorized to issue orders, notices, explanations, or circulars within their jurisdiction, provided these instruments remain consistent with the governing Act and rules.

The Commissioner of Customs (Valuation) has the authority to issue orders, notices, explanations, or circulars relevant to their jurisdiction, ensuring all such issuances are consistent with the Customs Act and associated rules.

All Commissioners of Customs are granted the power to issue orders, notices, explanations, or circulars within their respective jurisdictions, provided that such issuances do not conflict with the provisions of the Customs Act or the rules framed under it.
Director General: The Director General is authorized to issue orders, notices, explanations, or circulars within their jurisdiction, ensuring that these are consistent with the statutory requirements of the Customs Act and the rules made thereunder.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Repeals and amendments
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 220. Repeals and amendments.- The enactments specified in the 6[Fourth Schedule] are repealed or amended to the extent specified respectively in columns three and four thereof.

Fourth Schedule: The Fourth Schedule specifies the list of enactments that are subject to repeal or amendment.
The extent to which these specific laws are repealed or amended is detailed within the columns of this schedule.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Savings
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
221. Savings.- (1) Notwithstanding anything contained in section 6 of the General Clauses Act, 1897 ( X of 1897), anything done or any action taken under the repealed enactments in so far as it is not inconsistent with the provisions of this Act shall without prejudice to anything already done or any action already taken be deemed to have been done or taken under this Act:

Provided that nothing in this Act shall be so construed as to have the effect of enhancing the punishment of an offence committed before the commencement of this Act:

Provided further that where the period of limitations for the submission of an application or the filing of an appeal or revision prescribed under any of the repealed enactments had expired or had begun to run before the commencement of this Act the provisions of those enactments shall continue to apply to such limitation.

(2) The provisions of the General Clauses Act, 1897 (X of 1897), in particular, section 6, section 8 and section 24 thereof, shall apply to the repeal and re-enactment of the said enactments by this Act, subject to the provision of sub-section (1).

(3) Nothing in this Act shall affect any law for the time being in force relating to the constitution and powers of the trustees of any port or other port authority.

Customs Act 1969: This Act provides that actions taken under repealed enactments remain valid if they are consistent with the current provisions of this Act.
The Act ensures that no penalty for a prior offence is increased due to the commencement of this Act, maintaining the principle of non-retroactive punishment.
The Act clarifies that its provisions do not supersede existing laws concerning the constitution and operational powers of port authorities.
General Clauses Act 1897: The provisions of this Act, specifically regarding repeals and re-enactments, apply to the transition of laws under the Customs Act 1969.
Limitation of Legal Actions: If a period of limitation for filing applications, appeals, or revisions had already expired or commenced under repealed laws, those original time limits remain binding despite the new Act.
Port Authority: The Customs Act 1969 does not affect or alter the existing legal framework governing the constitution and functional powers of port authorities.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Removal of difficulties
processed_clauses.resolved_text: 222. Removal of difficulties.- If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, particularly in relation to the transition from the enactments repealed by this Act to the provisions of this Act the 1[Government] may, by general or special order made during the period of one year from the commencement of this Act direct such action to be taken as it considers necessary or expedient for the purpose of removing the difficulty.

Customs Act 1969: This clause provides the Government with the authority to resolve operational difficulties that may arise during the transition from previous legislation to the current Act.
The power to issue orders for the purpose of removing such difficulties is limited to a one-year period following the commencement of the Act.
Government: The Government is empowered to issue general or special orders to address and resolve any difficulties that arise while implementing the provisions of the Act.

processed_clauses.clause_title: Authentic Bangla Text
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
47[223.. Authentic Bangla Text.- There shall be an authentic Bangla text of this original Act:

Provided that in the event of conflict between the two texts, the original text shall prevail.]

Customs Act 1969: The law requires that there be an authentic version of the Act produced in the Bangla language.
In the event of a legal conflict or discrepancy between the Bangla text and the original text of the Act, the original text takes precedence.

processed_clauses.clause_title: THE THIRD SCHEDULE
processed_clauses.resolved_text:
48[ THE THIRD SCHEDULE ]

1. Regulation of proceedings for the detention and confiscation of the prohibited goods imported and intended to be exported, including verification of information relating to such goods, notices to be given to the owner or other parties, security for the custody or release of such goods, examination of evidence, reimbursement by the informant of expenses and damages caused by incorrect information supplied by him.

2. Cases in which the goods or material imported with a view to subsequent exportation or to be used in the production, manufacture, processing, repair or refitting to goods specified in the rule may be delivered without payment of the whole or part of the duty; and repayment of duty on such goods and material.

3. Valuation of the goods imported or intended to be exported; submission by the importer or exporter of information necessary for the proper valuation of the goods. and production of the relevant books and document by him; furnishing of information by the importer or relating to the sources, nature and amount of the funds or assets by which the goods were acquired or the consideration for which and the manner in which it was disposed of.

4. Determining denature spirit, and testing and denaturing of spirit.

5. Matters pertaining to draw back : drawback in respect of used goods, the amount of duty which shall be repaid as drawback on such goods, prohibition of drawback on any specified goods or class of goods; condition for the payment of drawback; limiting the period during which such goods must be exported; limiting the time during which drawback may be claimed.

6. The extent to which and the conditions subject to which drawback may be allowed on the imported material used in the manufacture of goods in 49[Bangladesh] which are exported.

7. Matters relating to port clearance or to departure of conveyances; grant of special pass permitting bulk to be broken; conditions relating to the grant of port clearance to the master of a vessel when the agent furnishes security for the delivery of export manifest and other documents.

8. Sealing of conveyances carrying transit goods and in other cases.

9. Marking of boats belonging to 50[Bangladeshi] ships and of other vessels not exceeding one hundred tons; prohibition, regulation and restriction of the playing of such boats and vessels; fees for licenses and registration of cargo boats.

10. Expenses to be charged when customs officer is specially employed to accompany the owner to the warehouse under section 93; Fees to be charged for permitting the owner of any goods to deal with them as provided in section 94.

11. Matters pertaining to the manufacturing and other operation carried on in the warehouse.

12. Transshipment and prohibition and regulation and restriction of transshipment of goods without payment of duty; power of officers of customs in that behalf ; and the fees for transshipment.

13. Export of frustrated cargo under section 138.

14. Transport of goods from one port of 51[Bangladesh] to another through foreign territory; condition as to the due arrival of such goods at the destination.

15. Conditions and restrictions applying to the transit of goods to a foreign territory without payment of duty;

16. Bill of Export.

17. Baggage of passengers and the crew; definition. declaration, custody, examinations, assessment and clearance of such baggage ; transit and transshipment of each baggage; circumstances and conditions under which such baggage or any specified class of goods included in such baggage would be exempt from duty; extent of such exemption.

18. Matter pertaining to the import or export of goods by post; examination, assessment, clearance, transit of transshipment of the goods so imported or to be exported.

19. Prevention of the taking out of 2[Bangladesh] of any coastal goods the export of which is dutiable of prohibited under this Act or any other law; prevention of the substitution of imported goods or export goods by coastal goods on board a vessel; prohibiting the conveyance of any specified class of goods generally, or to or between specified ports in a coastal vessel.

20. Power to be exercised by an officer stationed at a factory or building under section 176.

21. Licensing of agents: the form of the licence and fee payable therefor; the authority competent to grant the licence. the period of validity of the licence; qualifications of the licence; conditions and restrictions applying to the licence including furnishing of security; 52[circumstances in which penalty may be imposed on the licensee or licence may be suspended or revoked; appeals against the penalty or suspension or revocation of the licence.]

22. Matters pertaining to any business for the regulation of which a notification may be issued under section 212; the accounts and records to be maintained, and the information to be furnished, by persons engaged in such business.

53[22A.Reward under section217A.]

23. Any other matter necessary for giving effect to the provisions of this Act.

Third Schedule: This schedule provides the legislative framework for the Government to issue rules covering a wide range of operational, administrative, and enforcement matters under the Customs Act.
It serves as the enabling basis for subordinate regulations concerning the movement, clearance, and taxation of goods, the licensing of agents, and the exercise of powers by customs officers.
Prohibited Goods: The Third Schedule authorizes the regulation of proceedings for the detention and confiscation of prohibited goods imported or intended for export.
It covers verification procedures, notice requirements, security protocols for custody, and provisions for handling incorrect information supplied by informants.
Goods: The schedule provides for the valuation of imported or export goods, including the production of books and documents by the importer or exporter.
It also regulates goods imported for processing, manufacture, or repair, including conditions for duty exemptions and repayment of duty.
Importer: The schedule requires importers to furnish information regarding the sources and nature of funds used to acquire goods.
Importers are obligated to provide necessary documentation for proper valuation and compliance with customs procedures.
Exporter: Exporters are required to submit information necessary for the proper valuation of goods intended for export and must produce relevant books and documents upon request.
Warehouse: The schedule covers matters pertaining to manufacturing and other operations conducted within a warehouse.
It authorizes the charging of expenses when a customs officer is specially employed to accompany an owner to the warehouse and fees for permitting owners to deal with goods therein.
Port Clearance: The schedule regulates matters relating to port clearance and the departure of conveyances.
It sets out conditions for granting port clearance to the master of a vessel, including requirements for security regarding the delivery of manifests.
Conveyance: The schedule provides for the sealing of conveyances carrying transit goods and general regulation of vessel departures.
It also regulates the marking, licensing, and operation of cargo boats and smaller vessels.
Transshipment of Goods: The schedule governs the prohibition, regulation, and restriction of transshipment of goods without payment of duty.
It authorizes the collection of fees for transshipment activities and defines the powers of customs officers in overseeing such operations.
Frustrated Cargo: The schedule provides for the regulation of the export of frustrated cargo in accordance with specific sections of the Act.
Transit and Transshipment: The schedule details conditions and restrictions for the transit of goods to foreign territories without payment of duty.
It addresses the transport of goods between ports through foreign territory and ensures compliance regarding their arrival at the destination.
Bill of Export: The schedule explicitly includes the Bill of Export as a matter for regulatory provision.
Baggage: The schedule covers the definition, declaration, custody, examination, assessment, and clearance of passenger and crew baggage.
It regulates the transit and transshipment of baggage and defines the conditions under which baggage may be exempt from duty.
Coastal Goods: The schedule provides for the prevention of the illegal export of dutiable or prohibited coastal goods.
It includes measures to prevent the substitution of imported or export goods with coastal goods on board a vessel and regulates the conveyance of specific classes of goods between coastal ports.
Agent: The schedule mandates the licensing of agents, including the specification of fees, qualifications, and conditions of validity.
It provides for the imposition of penalties, suspension, or revocation of licenses and the right to appeal these administrative actions.
Officer of Customs: The schedule authorizes the exercise of specific powers by customs officers stationed at factories or buildings and defines their role in regulating transshipment.

Fourth Schedule: This schedule lists the specific enactments or parts thereof that are repealed upon the commencement of the Customs Act 1969.
Sea Customs Act 1878: The entire act is repealed by the Customs Act 1969.
Inland Bonded Warehouses Act 1896: The entire act is repealed by the Customs Act 1969.
Land Customs Act 1924: The entire act is repealed by the Customs Act 1969.
Tariff Act 1934: The entire act is repealed by the Customs Act 1969.
Civil Aviation Ordinance 1960: Section 14 of this ordinance is repealed by the Customs Act 1969.
